name: Bacillus coagulans
definition: GS1 Tagname Description: Bacillus coagulans is approved for veterinary purposes as GRAS by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Center for Veterinary Medicine, as well as by the European Union, and is listed by AAFCO for use as a direct-fed microbial in livestock production. It is often used in veterinary applications, especially as a probiotic in pigs, cattle, poultry, and shrimp. Many references to use of this bacterium in humans exist, especially in improving the vaginal flora, improving abdominal pain and bloating in irritable bowel syndrome patients, and increasing immune response to viral challenges. name: Glucosamine
definition:
GS1 Tagname Description: Glucosamine (C6H13NO5) is an amino sugar and a prominent precursor in the biochemical synthesis of glycosylated proteins and lipids. Glucosamine is part of the structure of the polysaccharides chitosan and chitin, which compose the exoskeletons of crustaceans and other arthropods, as well as the cell walls of fungi and many higher organisms. Glucosamine is one of the most abundant monosaccharides. It is produced commercially by the hydrolysis of crustacean exoskeletons or, less commonly, by fermentation of a grain such as corn or wheat.
Evidence for the effectiveness of glucosamine as a dietary supplement is mixed. In the United States, it is one of the most common dietary supplements used by adults that is neither a vitamin nor a mineral. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glucosamine - UOM for Nutrient Panel: - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms:

name: USDA Food and Nutrition Service
definition:
The Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) is an agency of USDA’s Food, Nutrition, and Consumer Services.

FNS works to end hunger and obesity through the administration of 15 federal nutrition assistance programs including WIC, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), and school meals.  In partnership with State and Tribal governments, FNS programs serve one in four Americans  during the course of a year. Working with public, private and non-profit partners, the mission is to increase food security and reduce hunger by providing children and low-income people access to food, a healthful diet and nutrition education in a way that supports American agriculture and inspires public confidence. No American should have to go hungry.   http://www.fns.usda.gov/

definition: Fruits & Veggies-More Matters is a health initiative focused on helping Americans increase fruit & vegetable consumption for better health. http://www.fruitsandveggiesmorematters.org/.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: 3-Every-Day of Dairy
definition: Consuming 3-Every-Day® of Dairy – three daily servings of milk, cheese, or yogurt – is an easy way for families to get a powerful punch of nutrients to help build stronger bones and healthy bodies and reduce the risk of osteoporosis. In addition, a growing body of research suggests that enjoying three servings of dairy foods a day as part of a nutrient-rich, balanced diet may help maintain a healthy weight. www.nationaldairycouncil.org
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: American Diabetes Association Food Exchange List
definition: If you have diabetes, it’s essential to have a road map for your diet. This road map is a meal plan, and you can either create it by yourself or enlist the help of a registered nutritionist, dietitian or certified diabetes educator. The goal of a meal plan exchange lists is to help control your blood sugar and lose weight by balancing the type and amount of food you eat. Diabetics should follow a diet low in carbohydrates, fat and calories. Exchange lists, which were created by the American Dietetic Association and the American Diabetes Association as a meal planning guide primarily for diabetics, are based on principles of good nutrition that apply to everyone. The foods within each group have similar amounts of calories, carbs, fats, and proteins, which allows for greater flexibility in choosing foods.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Weight Watchers
definition: The item meets criteria set forth by Weight Watchers (https://welcome.weightwatchers.com/) and is eligible for their weight management program.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Nutri-Score
definition: Nutri-Score was created by the French Health Ministry in order to introduce an independent measure of the nutritional quality of food products. The score itself is calculated based on the nutritional data and ingredients, and is displayed as a colored logo (green to red) and letters (A to E).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Smart Snacks
definition: Smart Snacks was established to help students get the nutrition they need to grow and learn during the school day. Any food or beverage sold to students at schools during the school day, other than those foods provided as part of the school meal program, must meet Smart Snack criteria as defined by the USDA Guide to Smart Snacks in Schools - https://fns-prod.azureedge.net/sites/default/files/resource-files/USDASmartSnacks_508_62019.pdf
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Health Star Rating
definition: The Health Star Rating is a front-of-pack labelling system that rates the overall nutritional profile of packaged food and assigns it a rating from ½ a star to 5 stars. It provides a quick, easy, standard way to compare similar packaged foods. The more stars, the healthier the choice. (http://healthstarrating.gov.au)
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Atkins 20
definition: The Atkins 20 is a low carbohydrate-keto diet which is split into four phases of carbohydrate control.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Atkins 40
definition: Atkins 40 is a low carb diet plan based on portion control and eating 40 grams net carbs per day.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Atkins 100
definition: Atkins 100 is a low carb plan based on portion control and eating 100 grams of net carbs per day.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: HFSS (High in fat, sugar or salt)
definition: The UK government program to reduce childhood obesity includes restrictions in the promotion of food and drink products classified as high in fat, sugar or salt (HFSS) under the UK Department of Health 2004 nutritional profile model. The intent is that the industry will use the nutritional profile model to calculate the score and convey the numeric result.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Concentrated/Dried fruit and vegetables
definition: Concentrated/dried fruit or vegetables (e.g. dried fruit or tomato paste)
codeListDefinition: Allows to identify the groups of main ingredients contained in the product to better highlight them for the consumer.

name: Fruits, vegetables, legumes and nuts
definition: Identifies the quantity of fruits, vegetables, legumes and nuts contained in the recipe of the product.
codeListDefinition: Allows to identify the groups of main ingredients contained in the product to better highlight them for the consumer.

name: Whole grain
definition: The amount of whole unprocessed grains. A whole grain is a grain of any cereal and pseudo-cereal that contains the endosperm, germ, and bran.
codeListDefinition: Allows to identify the groups of main ingredients contained in the product to better highlight them for the consumer.

name: Registered
definition: The brand or product is registered with the associated nutritional program.
codeListDefinition: A code specifying the status of the brand or product with the nutritional program. Example: REGISTERED - the brand of a product is registered for Nutri-Score at the French Health Ministry.

name: Registered but not active
definition: The brand or product is registered with the nutritional program, but has not yet completed all stages of implementation. (e.g. the nutrional score is not labeled on the packaging yet.)
codeListDefinition: A code specifying the status of the brand or product with the nutritional program. Example: REGISTERED - the brand of a product is registered for Nutri-Score at the French Health Ministry.

name: Not registered
definition: The brand or product has not been registered with the associated nutritional program.
codeListDefinition: A code specifying the status of the brand or product with the nutritional program. Example: REGISTERED - the brand of a product is registered for Nutri-Score at the French Health Ministry.

name: Main content page count
definition: The highest-numbered page in a single numbered sequence of main content, usually the highest Arabic-numbered page in a book; or, for books without page numbers or (rarely) with multiple numbered sequences of main content, the total number of pages that carry the main content of the book. This is the preferred page count for most books for the general reader. For books with substantial front and/or back matter, include also Front matter and Back matter page counts, or Total numbered pages.

definition: Number of words of natural language text
codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Front matter page count
definition: The total number of numbered (usually Roman-numbered) pages that precede the main content of a book. This usually consists of an introduction, preface, foreword, etc.
codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Back matter page count
definition: The total number of numbered (usually Roman-numbered) pages that follow the main content of a book. This usually consists of an afterword, appendices, endnotes, index, etc.
codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Total numbered pages
definition: The sum of all Roman- and Arabic-numbered pages.
codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Production page count
definition: The total number of pages in a book, including unnumbered pages, front matter, back matter, etc. This includes any blank pages at the back that carry no content and are present only for convenience of printing and binding
codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Absolute page count
definition: The total number of pages of the book counting the cover as page 1. This page count type should be used only for digital publications delivered with fixed pagination.
codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Number of pages in print counterpart
definition: The total number of pages in the print counterpart of a digital product delivered without fixed pagination.
codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Duration

codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Notional number of pages in digital product
definition: An estimate of the number of 'pages' in a digital product delivered without fixed pagination, and with no print counterpart, given as an indication of the size of the work.
codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Content page count
definition: The sum of all Roman- and Arabic-numbered and contentful unnumbered pages.
codeListDefinition: Based on ONIX List 23

name: Total unnumbered insert page count
definition: The total number of unnumbered pages with content inserted within the main content of a book - for example inserts/plate sections that are not numbered.

name: Full
definition: Full coverage is very opaque, and used to cover birthmarks, vitiligo, hyperpigmentation and scars. It is sometimes referred to as “corrective” or “camouflage” make-up. Products with full or high coverage contain over 15% pigment.
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Light
definition: Light can cover unevenness and slight blotchiness, but is not opaque enough to cover freckles. Products with light coverage have 5-10 percent pigment.
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Medium
definition: Medium coverage can cover freckles, discolorations, blotchiness, and red marks left by pimples. Products with medium coverage have 10-15 percent pigment.
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Sheer
definition: Sheer is the most transparent and contains the least amount of pigment. It will not hide discolorations on the skin but it can minimize the contrast between the discoloration and the rest of the skin tone. Products with sheer coverage have less than 5 percent pigment.
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Extremely opaque
definition: Extremely opaque also known as blackout, light doesn't pass through and textile heavier than very opaque. 100+ denier
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Opaque
definition: Opaque materials do not allow light to pass through or penetrate them. 41-69 denier
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Semi-opaque
definition: Translucent Fabric Otherwise known as semi – opaque, this group of fabrics consists of materials that are woven in a solid form and material with an open weave which includes holes and patterns. 21-40 denier
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Sheer
definition: Sheer fabrics are widely used in dressmaking and decoration. Examples: Chiffon, georgette, organza and organdy, fine mesh, netting. 10-20 denier
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Very opaque
definition: Very opaque light doesn't pass through and textile heavier than opaque. 70-99 denier
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Very sheer
definition: Textile which is very thin, almost transparent. <5-9 Denier
codeListDefinition: A code to describe the opacity achieved by the product. The codes may vary by product type. Examples Cosmetics, Glass, Paints and Wood Stains. Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Active
definition: Is orderable and returnable unless "Is Trade Item Returnable" = "FALSE".
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cut Out
definition: Is not orderable and is returnable unless the one-way flag is set to "yes".
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Deleted
definition: Not orderable and not returnable.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Hold
definition: Temporarily unavailable but is still returnable unless the one-way flag is set to "yes".
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: EPA
definition: EPA – US Environmental Protection Agency
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Demeter-Bund
definition: Demeter-Bund - The Demeter movement as an entrepreneurial network promotes the development of bio-dynamic economy, to secure the livelihoods of the world and to strengthen the positive people in his ministry. In cooperation contribute producers, processors, traders and consumers in partnership to shape the market.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: GÄA
definition:
GÄA - Gäa is a diverse farming association for farmers, processors and traders inside.Focal point is Germany. Gäa is a special design for the structure of the organic farming. 
Biokreis- The Biokreis is an association for organic farming. Currently more than 800 farms, 80 and 200 processors, consumers are members of Biokreis, committed to working together on more than 33,000 for organic and sustainable farming.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Naturland
definition: Naturland - Naturland is active the world over in promoting organic agriculture. Its members are farmers who produce a wide range of valuable products: coffee from Mexico and Peru, olive oil from Greece, tea from the slopes of India’s mountains, pineapple and other tropical fruit from Uganda, spices from Sri Lanka. Organic agriculture safeguards the existence of smallholders and helps with the sustainable management of what are often fragile ecosystems. On a global scale, over 50,000 Naturland farmers are cultivating an area of over 142,000 hectares.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Biopark
definition: Biopark - Biopark is an organic farmers’ association based in the North of Germany, in Mecklenburg-Vorpommerania.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Ecovin
definition: Ecovin - ECOVIN Federation Organic Viticulture Association: ECOVIN largest merger in 1985 as ecologically-working wine estates in Germany was founded. Approximately 220 member companies currently manage 1,600 hectares of vineyards in 11 German wine-growing areas.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: IFOAM
definition: IFOAM - The International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements (IFOAM) is a grassroots and democratic organisation that currently unites 750 member organisations in 116 countries. Note: this value will be deleted in the future and should not be used.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Demeter International
definition: Demeter International Demeter-International e. V. is a non profit organisation and its member organisations work together in the spirit of an international confederation with democratic principles. Membership requires a functioning Demeter certification programme.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bioland
definition: Bioland: The leading organic farmers' association in Germany for the economy of organic-based businesses without synthetic pesticides and synthetic chemical nitrogen fertilizer. The animals are kept humanely and processed food carefully. This provides an environmentally sound and sustainable food production. http://www.bioland.de.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: QCS
definition: Quality Certification Services. Note: this value will be deleted in the future and should not be used.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: FSA
definition: FSA – UK Food Standards Agency
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: WSDA
definition: Washington State Dept. of Agriculture. Note: this value will be deleted in the future and should not be used.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: CFIA - Organic Regime
definition: The Canada Organic Regime is the Government of Canada's response to requests by the organic sector and consumers to develop a regulated system for organic agricultural products. The Organic Products Regulations define specific requirements for organic products to be labelled as organic or that bear the Canada Organic logo. URL: http://www.inspection.gc.ca/food/organic-products/labelling-and-general-information/certified-choice/eng/1328082717777/1328082783032
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: EU Commission
definition: The European Union Commission.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: The Organic Industry Standards and Certification Council (OISCC)
definition: OISCC - The Organic Industry Standards and Certification Council maintains the Australian National Standard for Organic and Biodynamic Produce, to ensure continued consumer confidence and International market access.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Australian Certified Organic (ACO)
definition: ACO - Australian Certified Organic is Australia’s largest certifier for organic and biodynamic produce and has over 1500 operators within its certification system. ACO is a not for profit fully-owned subsidiary of Australia Organic Ltd.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: National Association for Sustainable Agriculture (NASAA)
definition: NASAA Certified Organic (NCO) is a fully-owned subsidiary of The National Association for Sustainable Agriculture, Australia who provides the certification services.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: OFC
definition: OFC - The Organic Food Chain provides certification services in accordance with the National Standard for Organic and Bio-Dynamic Produce and other international organic certification standards.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: AUS-QUAL
definition: AUS-QUAL is a certification body accredited by JAS-ANZ, providing conformity assessment services for quality management and food safety (HACCP) management systems, as well as Product Cortication Systems for the wider Australian and New Zealand agricultural, horticultural and secondary processing sectors.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: BDRI
definition:
The Bio-Dynamic Research Institute, founded in 1957, is involved in research and practical development of the Australian DEMETER Bio-Dynamic Method of Agriculture. In 1967 it was vested with the rights and supervision of the DEMETER Trademark in Australia.
Part of this role is the certification of DEMETER quality products.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: SFQ
definition: Safe Food Production Queensland  works in partnership with the Department of Agriculture and Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF) and Queensland Health (QH) across the entire food chain, to ensure Queensland's food supply is safe.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: FDA
definition: FDA – US Food and Drug Agency
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Danish Veterinary and Food Administration (DVFA)
definition:
​The Danish Veterinary and Food Administration (DVFA) is part of the Ministry of Environment and Food. DVFA is responsible for food safety and health from farm to fork and maintains a list of Danish food companies, aquacultural farms etc. subject to organic inspection.
Only authorities under the Ministry of Environment and Food carry out inspection under the government rules for organic production. The Danish AgriFish Agency inspects ​the primary production, while the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration (DVFA) inspects food companies.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Ökohöfe
definition: Verbund Ökohöfe e.V. is an organic cultivation association based in Wanzleben in the Magdeburg Börde region
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bayerisches Bio-Siegel
definition: The biolabel of the Bavarian State Ministry for Food, Agriculture and Forestry meets the wish of consumers for a high quality of organic products and traceable origin. Only those products whose organic quality standards extend far beyond the statutory regulations and originate from the stated regions are permitted to bear this quality seal. Try out convincing organic products yourself, safe in the knowledge of their place of origin.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bio Baden-Württemberg
definition: The products marked with the bio-symbol Baden-Württemberg are regional organic foods with traceable origin. The use or labelling is based on the ecological standards of the EC eco-regulation supplemented by the requirement that the products have to be produced in fully converted farms and partly also to the stricter requirements of the ecological cultivation associations
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Stichting EKO keurmerk
definition: The EKO Certification Foundation is an independent private foundation established in 2012. The foundation has no profit objective. The EKO label for foods has been around for 30 years, and most people know as a hallmark for organic foods. The EKO certificate has been the owner of this collective mark. With the advent of the European Ecolabel (the green leaf with the asterisks), EKO has been given the opportunity to develop further. Producers should be in addition to biologically certified, also carry out additional efforts in the area of ​​sustainability.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: International Foundation for Organic Agriculture

name: Made with Canadian Mustard Seeds
definition: The claim "Canadian" is considered to be the same as a "Product of Canada" claim. As such, all or virtually all major ingredients, processing, and labour used to make the food product must be Canadian. For example, the claim "Canadian" on a container of frozen lasagna would mean that the food meets the "Product of Canada" criteria
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Processed in Canada
definition: To describe a food which has been entirely processed in Canada
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Product of Canada
definition: A food product may use the claim "Product of Canada" when all or virtually all major ingredients, processing, and labour used to make the food product are Canadian. This means that all the significant ingredients in a food product are Canadian in origin and that non-Canadian material is negligible.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Proudly Canadian

name: Absence of Eggs and Milk is a Certified Allergen Control (CAC)

name: Intermediate Bulk Container, rigid plastic
definition:
A Rigid Intermediate Bulk Container (RIBC) that is attached to a pallet or has the pallet integrated into the RIBC. The container is used for the transport and storage of fluids and other bulk materials. The construction of the IBC container and the materials used are chosen depending on the application.  There are various types available in the market place.
Foldable (collapsible) IBC Container,
Plastic composite IBC Container,
Wire Cage IBC Container,
Steel IBC Container, and
Stainless steel IBC Container.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Aerosol
definition: A gas-tight, pressure-resistant container with a valve and propellant. When the valve is opened, propellant forces the product from the container in a fine or coarse spray pattern or stream. (e.g., a spray can dispensing paint, furniture polish, etc, under pressure). It does not include atomizers, because atomizers do not rely on a pressurised container to propel product from the container.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Ampoule
definition: A relatively small container in tube shape, the end of which is drawn into a stem and closed by fusion after filling. The bottom may be flat, convex, or drawn out. An ampule is opened by breaking the stem.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Barrel
definition: A cylindrical packaging whose bottom end is permanently fixed to the body and top end (head) is either removable or non-removable.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bag in Box
definition: Bag-In-Box or BIB is a type of container for the storage and transportation of liquids. It consists of a strong bladder, usually seated inside a corrugated fibreboard box. The box and internal bag can be fused together. In most cases there is nozzle or valve fixed to the bag. The nozzle can be connected easily to a dispensing installation or the valve allows for convenient dispensing.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bag
definition: A preformed, flexible container, generally enclosed on all but one side, which forms an opening that may or may not be sealed after filling.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bucket
definition: A container, usually cylindrical, can be equipped with a lid and a handle. (e.g., a pail made of metal, plastic, or other appropriate material).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Basket
definition: A semi rigid container usually open at the top traditionally used for gathering, shipping and marketing agricultural products.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bottle
definition: A container having a round neck of relatively smaller diameter than the body, as compared with a jar, and an opening capable of holding a closure for retention of the contents. The cross section of the bottle may be round, oval, square, oblong, or a combination of these.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Blister pack
definition: A type of packaging in which the item is secured between a cavity or pocket made from a formable web, usually transparent, and a flat backing.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Brick
definition: A rectangular-shaped, stackable package designed primarily for liquids such as juice or milk
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Box
definition: A non-specific term used to refer to a rigid container with closed faces that completely enclose its contents.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cage
definition: A container enclosed on at least one side by a grating of wires or bars that lets in air and light.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Chub
definition: A chub or a chub pack is a type of container formed by a tube of flexible, non-edible packaging material. The cylindrical package has the appearance of a sausage with the ends sealed by metal crimps or clips, e.g. for sausages (artificial intestine).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Card
definition: A flat package to which the product is hung or attached for display.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Clam Shell
definition: A one-piece container consisting of two halves joined by a hinge area which allows the structure to come together to close. Clamshells get their name from their appearance to the shell of a clam, which it resembles both in form and function.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Can/Tin
definition: A metallic and generally cylindrical container of unspecified size which can be used for items of consumer and institutional sizes.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cartridge
definition: A container holding an item or substance, designed for insertion into a mechanism. Examples: Ink, beverage syrup, silicone sealant for construction.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Crate
definition: A non-specific term usually referring to a rigid three- dimensional container with semi-closed faces that enclose its contents for shipment or storage. Crates could have an open or closed top and may have internal divers. Even though some crates might be reused or become resealed they could also be disposable depending on the product hierarchy.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Case
definition: A non-specific term for a container designed to hold, house, and sheath or encase its content while protecting it during distribution, storage and/or exhibition. Cases are mostly intended to store and preserve its contents during the product's entire lifetime.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Carton
definition: A non-specific term for an open or re-closable container used mostly for perishable foods (e.g. eggs, or fruit).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cup/Tub/Bowl
definition: A flat-bottomed container that has a base of any shape and which may or not be closed with a lid. These containers are typically used to contain mostly (but not exclusively) foods such as ice cream, margarine, yogurt, sour cream, confections, etc.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cylinder
definition: A rigid cylindrical container with straight sides and circular ends of equal size.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Envelope
definition: A predominantly flat container of flexible material having only two faces, and joined at three edges to form an enclosure. The non-joined edge provides a filling opening, which may later be closed by a gummed or adhesive flap, heat seal, tie string, metal clasp, or other methods.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Gable Top
definition: A rectangular-shaped, non-stackable package designed primarily for liquids such as juice or milk
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Jug
definition: A container, normally cylindrical, with a handle and/or a lid or spout for holding and pouring liquids
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Jar
definition: A rigid container with a large opening, which is used to store products, e.g., jams, cosmetics.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Multipack
definition: A bundle of products held together for ease of carriage by the consumer. A multipack is always a consumer unit.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Not packed
definition: The item is provided without packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Net
definition: A container of meshwork material made from threads or strips twisted or woven to form a regular pattern with spaces between the threads that is used for holding, carrying, trapping, or confining something.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Pallet Box
definition: A three-dimensional container which either has a pallet platform permanently attached at its base or alternatively requires a platform for its handling and storage as due to its constitution it cannot be handled without it. The characteristics of the platform should be specified using the pallet type code list
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Peel Pack
definition: A package used for hygienic/sterile products which may be torn open without touching the product inside.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Pouch
definition: A preformed, flexible container, generally enclosed with a gusset seal at the bottom of the pack can be shaped/arranged to allow the pack to stand on shelf.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Pot
definition: A flat-bottomed container that has a base of any shape and which may or not be closed with a lid. Pots may be used for a wide array of products such as cosmetics, food/liquids, dairy products, plants.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Tray
definition: A shallow container, which may or may not have a cover, used for displaying or carrying items.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Packed, unspecified
definition: Packaging of the product (or products) is currently not on the list. Use this code when no suitable options are available and only while a Change Request is approved for the proper packaging type.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Pallet
definition: A platform used to hold or transport unit loads.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Rack
definition: A non specific term identifying a framework or stand for carrying, holding, or storing items. Commonly on wheels and primarily used in the logistical functions to deliver items such as hanging garments, or items on shelves such as dairy products and bakery items and flowers.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Reel
definition: A spool on which thread, wire, film, etc, is wound. Any device on which a material may be wound. Usually has flanged ends and is used for shipping or processing purposes.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Roll
definition: Roll
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Stretchwrapped
definition: In packaging, a high-tensile film, stretched and wrapped repeatedly around an item or group of items to secure and maintain unit integrity. The use of stretch film to tightly wrap a package or a unit load in order to bind, protect and immobilize it for further handling or shipping.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Shrinkwrapped
definition: In packaging, a film around an item or group of items which is heated causing the film to shrink, securing the unit integrity. The use of shrunken film to tightly wrap a package or a unit load in order to bind, protect and immobilize it for further handling or shipping.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Sleeve
definition: A sleeve or banderole that is open-ended and is slid over the contents for protection or presentation.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Tube
definition: A cylindrical container sealed on one end that could be closed with a cap or dispenser on the other end.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Wire
definition: A packaging in the form of very flexible thread or slender rod.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Wrapper
definition: The process of enclosing all or part of an item with layer(s) of flexible wrapping material (e.g., for an individually packed ice cream, or for chocolate eggs wrapped in foil). Includes gas-tight packs (e.g. for sausages). Does not include items which are shrink-wrapped or vacuum-packed.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Banded package
definition: Something used to bind, tie, or encircle the item or its packaging to secure and maintain unit integrity.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Flexible Intermediate Bulk Container
definition: A non-rigid container used for transport and storage of fluids and other bulk materials. The construction of the IBC container and the materials used are chosen depending on the application.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Known
definition: Recognized, familiar, or within the scope of knowledge
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Source Certified
definition: The source has been certified.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: UnKnown
definition: Not known or familiar.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Base to stand up vertically
definition: A general term applied to the support or pedestal of an object.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Beams
definition: Long sturdy piece of squared timber or metal used in house-building etc.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bung seals
definition: A bung is an apparatus used to seal a container, such as a bottle, barrel or tube. A bung is partially inserted inside the container to act as a seal.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Butterfly Tap
definition: Tap for Bag in box. Lifted for function.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Can End 360
definition: A seal on  a e.g.  aluminium can where the entire lid can be removed.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cap
definition: A cap that seals a bottle or other form of packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Carriers
definition: A device of various types attached to or hung from trolleys to support the load.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Champagne cork and cage - natural
definition: Known as a muselet, a wire cage that fits over the cork of a bottle of champagne, sparkling wine or beer to prevent the cork from emerging under the pressure of the carbonated contents. Made of natural materials.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Champagne cork and cage - synthetic
definition: Known as a muselet, a wire cage that fits over the cork of a bottle of champagne, sparkling wine or beer to prevent the cork from emerging under the pressure of the carbonated contents. Made of synthetic materials.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Consumption utensil
definition: An item which allows the user to extract and/or consume the content of a container or product (straws, spoons, ice cream stick).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Core
definition: A tubular shape around which flexible material such as plastic film or paper are wound for purposes of transport and handling.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cork Agglomerate
definition: Cork cylinders made of natural cork granules which have been joined together using synthetic or natural binding agents that are moulded into shape.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cork Alternative
definition: Cork cylinders made of natural cork granules combined with food grade polymers, resins and binding agents that are moulded into shape.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cork Stopper
definition: Reclosable cork with top. Opened by hand.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: A-coupler
definition: Coupling to brewery barrel, type A.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: D-coupler
definition: Coupling to brewery barrel, type D.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: G-coupler
definition: Coupling to brewery barrel, type G.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: M-coupler
definition: Coupling to brewery barrel, type M.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: S-coupler
definition: Coupling to brewery barrel, type S.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: S3-coupler
definition: Coupling to brewery barrel, type S3.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: U-coupler
definition: Coupling to brewery barrel, type U.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Creel
definition: A creel is a device for holding the required number of roving spools or other supply packages of reinforcement fibers for Fiber Reinforced Plastics manufacturing. This device holds the rovings in the desired position for unwinding in continuous processes like Pultrusion and Filament Winding.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Crown Cap
definition: Closure of, e.g. glass bottles that need tools to open
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Crown ring pull
definition: Ring pull main feature is the easy to open mechanism being metal or plastic ring attached to the crown and lying flatly (parallel) to bottle neck. One opens the crown by pulling the ring and taking off the crown from the bottle mouth. No opening tool as bottle opener is required. A crown ring pull bottle cap is usually made of aluminium
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Edge Protection
definition: A right-angle piece placed over the outermost perimeter edges of a container to distribute pressure and prevent collapse or cutting from banding, strapping, or handling.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Flap
definition: A piece of material, hinged or attached only on one side, that covers an opening or hangs down from the packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Glass Cork
definition: Cork made of glass. Opened by hand.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Handles
definition: A grip attached to an object for using or moving the object, usually with the hands.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Inner containers
definition: Any container inside an outer container used to pack or transport e.g. dairy or meat products.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Integrated tap to brewery barrel
definition: The tap is integrated into the barrel, therefore does not require a coupling connector.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Internal Dividers
definition: An internal divider is an object, either flat or custom-shaped, used to separate the content of a container or to prevent the content from mixing.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Key k coupler
definition: Coupling to a barrel, type key keg.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Labels
definition: A label is a piece of paper, polymer, cloth, metal, or other material affixed to a container or article (or printed directly upon it), which usually carries information about the article to which it has been attached.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Laser Branded
definition: The product has not a physical packaging, but is directly laser marked in the product skin.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Lid
definition: In packaging, the top or bottom of a container, usually the part that closes the opening; may also be known as cap, over, or top
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Inner Coating or liners
definition: An internal chamber within a container which separates the content of the container from the walls. Inner liners provide additional isolation and protection to the content of a container. Sometimes coatings of certain materials may be applied as an alternative to inner liners.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Large Opening End (LOE)
definition: A metal lid closure scored and has a tab when pulled, opens the container without dislodging the closure. The most common seal of aluminium can.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Lightning stopper swing-top (LSST)
definition: The LSST is a pin with a spring and a toggle lever principle, usually made of porcelain or plastic, with a sealing ring, mainly for closing bottles. Opening and closing can be done by hand as often as desired and does not require any aid such as a bottle opener. Also known as a flip-top.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Lug
definition: A small indentation or raised portion on the surface of a bottle, provided as an indexing means for operations such as multi-pass decoration or labeling.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Microwave Suitable
definition: Product packaging suitable for its use in a microwave oven.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Natural cork
definition: Cork made of natural cork. Cork is the outer bark of the cork oak tree (Quercus suber L.).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Nesting Edges

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: A methodology used to hinder, or deter unauthorized access to a device.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: The process by which a sterile (aseptic) product (typically food or pharmaceutical) is packaged in a sterile container in a way which maintains sterility.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: A device for reducing a liquid to a fine spray. (e.g., medicine, perfume, etc). An atomizer does not rely on a pressurised container for the propellant.

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: Covered with a material (paraffin, wax) that protects the product or packaging.

definition: Content has been pressed together to the maximum possible way.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: A device or mechanism to supply or extract contents.

name: Flexible

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: Packaging is wrapped in a decorative way for the purposes of the consumer giving it as a gift.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Hygienic

Example: A load carrier that is designed so that the HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) cleaning standard can be applied and the load carrier is therefore suitable for the transport and storage of food.

definition: Thermal carry container designed for the carriage of temperature controlled goods such as vaccines, pharmaceuticals, and medicines.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: The practice of modifying the composition of the internal atmosphere of a package, (commonly food packages, and drugs) in order to improve the shelf life.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: A barrier packaging material for an infusion solution, i.e., oxygen.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: A section of the packaging can be detached with ease in order to have access to the content or product, e.g. peel-off Lids used for packing Milk, Coffee and Cacao Powder.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: The package is equipped to be hung up on a hook".

definition: Functionality to keep from being damaged, attacked, stolen, or injured; guard.

name: Reclosable
definition: Packaging designed to allow item to be reclosed after being opened.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: A component is added to a container for a particular application to lend additional support under severe applications.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Rigid
definition: Packaging designed so the shape remains unchanged when the product is added or removed.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: Packaging is designed to prevent leaking of the content specially when it is on powdered or liquid state.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: The packaging is designed to show when there has been some interference with the original sealing or configuration of the packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: Packaging in containers, either rigid or flexible, from which substantially all gases have been removed prior to final sealing of the container.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

definition: Coated with materials that make the packaging impervious to the effects of water.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Label on packaging
definition: A label with the product information is attached to the packaging material.
codeListDefinition: The type of text coverage of a packaging, e.g. Label, Printed on packaging.

name: Printed and label on packaging
definition: Physically printed on and a label attached to the packaging material containing the product information.
codeListDefinition: The type of text coverage of a packaging, e.g. Label, Printed on packaging.

name: Printed on packaging
definition: The product information is physically printed on the packaging material.
codeListDefinition: The type of text coverage of a packaging, e.g. Label, Printed on packaging.

name: Primary
definition: Constitutes the packaging designed to come into direct contact with the product.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Secondary
definition: Groups a given number of primary packaging units together into a convenient unit at the point of sale.  Secondary packaging typically has one of two roles:  it can be a convenient means to replenish the shelves; or it can group primary packaging units into a package for purchase.  It can be removed without affecting the product’s properties and generally defines the unit handled by the retailer
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Tertiary
definition: Is designed to ensure damage free handling and transport of a number of sales or grouped packages.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: 100 Percent Canadian Milk
definition: The use of a "100% Canadian Milk" or "100% Canadian Dairy" claim, with or without logos, vignettes etc., when used on dairy products, indicates all of the dairy ingredients in the product are derived from Canadian sources.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: 100% Veganskt
definition: 100% Veganskt (Vegan) is certified by Djurens rätt (Animal rights) and shows that the product does not contain animal ingredients.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Three-peak mountain snowflake (3PMSF)
definition: A three-peak mountain snowflake (3PMSF) symbol branded on a tire's sidewall indicates the tire meets required performance criteria in snow testing to be considered severe snow service-rated. Originally used as a designation for winter tires, the 3PMSF symbol is now featured on some all-season and all-terrain tires with snow performance that meets the testing criteria. (UNECE Regulation 117, (EC) 661/2009)
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Art And Creative Materials Institute, Inc.

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: ADCCPA

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: AFIA Pet Food Facility
definition: AFIA Pet Food Ingredient Facility Certification Program is launched by the American Feed Industry Association and administered by the Safe Quality Food Institute (SQFI). The program builds upon the domestic Safe Feed/Safe Food program, but is designed to meet the safety issues specifically related to the manufacturing of pet food.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: BIO Agency
definition: The BIO Agency is a public interest group whose mission is to develop and promote organic agriculture.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: AGRI Confiance
definition:
Where do the food products come from? How and by whom are they produced? Are they respectful of the environment?
It is to answer all these questions that Agri Confiance® was created in 1992. A collective approach of the producers organized in cooperative, engaged for a sustainable agriculture and for each one of us. A controlled engagement. An ambition. A movement. For there to be trust between us.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Agri Natura
definition: Certification for meat out of integrated production based on principles of IP-Suisse. Label owned by Ernst Sutter AG.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Agriculture Biologique
definition: France's national logo for organic products since 1985. Organic products carrying the logo must contain more than 95 percent organic components and be produced or processed within the EU, and were certified by one of the inspection bodies accredited according to EN 45011.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Air cleaner performance standard, e.g., humidifier
definition: The Association of Home Appliance Manufacturers (AHAM) is an organization that verifies the volume, energy and in some cases, performance, of many common household appliances. Since 1967, we've used outside laboratories to test products, and today you'll find the AHAM Verified Mark on all products included in our program – making comparing products easier for you
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: A.I.S.E
definition: A.I.S.E., the international Association for Soaps, Detergents and Maintenance Products is the official representative body of this industry in Europe.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: A.I.S.E 2005
definition: The International Association for Soaps, Detergents and Maintenance Products: This Charter logo on a product means that the company placing this product on the market is committed to the industry Charter for Sustainable Cleaning, and that the company has successfully complied with the Charter Sustainability Procedures. Consumers and professional users who see this logo on a product can be assured that the company making this product is voluntarily committed to delivering continual improvements in safety, environmental friendliness and other key aspects of sustainability. Only those companies that have signed up to the Charter, and meet the licensing conditions, are permitted to use it.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: A.I.S.E 2010
definition: The International Association for Soaps, Detergents and Maintenance Products This logo will certify that the company which manufactured the product is following Charter update 2010 sustainability principles.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: The A.I.S.E. 2020 mark for brands
definition: The new mark certifies that your brand meets all Charter product sustainability standards, in addition to the manufacturing requirements (ISO 14025 standard for Type III environmental labels and declarations).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: The A.I.S.E. 2020 mark for companies
definition: This new mark certifies that your organisation meets the Charter company sustainability standards in their manufacturing facilities (ISO 14025 standard for Type III environmental labels and declarations).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Atlanta Kashrus Commission Certification

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Wines of Alentejo Sustainability Programme
definition: The purpose of the WASP (Wines of Alentejo Sustainability Programme) is to align the sector's competitiveness with environmental, economic and social objectives, thus creating opportunities based on an integrated and sustainably oriented strategy. The certification of sustainable wine production is the guarantee that an independent evaluation, by a third party credentialed according to the Portuguese Quality System, confirms that good sustainability practices have been implemented. It is an important source of information to assess, guarantee and improve the environmental and socio-economic conditions of the industry.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Alimentation du tout petit
definition:
The "childhood food" symbol guarantees that the product complies with French and European regulatory requirements. In addition to perfectly meeting the special nutritional needs of children from birth to 3 years old, the product meets very strict safety standards.

Ingredient quality, strict monitoring of contaminants and microbiological risks, packaging composition... my child's meal is combed through to make sure everything is fine.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Aliments du Quebec
definition: Aliments du Québec is an organization whose mission is to promote Quebec agri-food products.  Promotional activities, brand identification at the points-of-sale and special events are all ways to inform consumers about the availability of Quebec food products
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Aliments du Quebec BIO
definition: Aliments du Québec is the holder of the unique label of origin for Quebec food products, recognized by the whole agri-food industry, we manage two certifications
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: AOP (Appellation d'Orgine Protegee)
definition: For products with an AOP (Appellation d’Origine Protégée), everything from the raw material for processing to the end product comes from a clearly defined region of origin. AOP is a quality mark protected by Swiss law, e.g. Emmentaler AOP. After registration by the Swiss Federal Office for Agriculture, the protected designation may only be used for products that meets the origin, process and quality requirements of the specifications. Independent certification bodies monitor their compliance.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Appellation Origine Controlee
definition:
The registered designation of origin (AOC) is a label allowing to identify a product whose manufacturing stages (production and processing) are carried out in the same geographical area and according to recognized know-how. It is the combination of a physical and biological environment with a traditional human community which bases the specificity of an AOC product, with definition in a specification.

The French AOC is an official French label that meets the criteria of the European Protected Designation of Origin (PDO). In France, since 2012, for products other than wine, the term AOC is replaced by AOP as soon as the product is registered at the European level.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Approved by Asthma Allergy Nordic

An ATG is a favourable review of one particular building product of one manufacturer for a particular application. It's all about systems, innovative products and products that contain multiple components.

definition: Austria Bio Garantie GMBH (ABG) is Austria's leading inspection body. It conducts inspections throughout Austria at all levels of the organic production chain (farmers-processors-traders-import/export) as well as in different foreign countries.

name: Organic Certifying Body – Province of British Columbia Certified Organic, British Columbia Association for Regenerative Agriculture (BCARA), Canada
definition: BCARA is accredited by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) as a certification body that certifies organic products under the Canada Organic Regime. Products certified under the Canada Organic Regime can be sold inter-provincially and internationally to countries that have equivalency agreements with Canada. The Organic Products Regulations require mandatory certification to the current National Organic Standard for agricultural products represented as organic in international and inter-provincial trade, or that bear the federal organic agricultural product legend (or federal logo).

definition: The government animal-welfare label will initially be for pork, but it will later be expanded to cover meat from other animals. name: BENOR
definition: BENOR stands for BElgian NORm and points out that a product is according to Belgian standards. Mainly for building materials in road construction.

name: Berchtesgadener Land

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Best Aquaculture Practices
definition:
The Best Aquaculture Practices Certified (BAP Certified) mark on retail packaging tells consumers that seafood came from BAP certified aquaculture facilities.
The Best Aquaculture Practices standards, developed by the Global Aquaculture Alliance, form the basis for BAP certification. The standards specifically protect biodiversity and worker rights within a program that addresses environmental, social, food safety and traceability issues throughout producers' operations.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Best Aquaculture Practices 2 Stars
definition: 2 Star BAP accreditation. The BAP program is the world’s most comprehensive third-party certification system for aquaculture facilities, addressing every key element of responsible aquaculture, including environmental responsibility, social responsibility, food safety, animal welfare, traceability and more. BAP standards encompassing the entire aquaculture production chain, including farms, processing plants, hatcheries and feed mills.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Best Aquaculture Practices 3 Stars
definition: 3 Star BAP accreditation. The BAP program is the world’s most comprehensive third-party certification system for aquaculture facilities, addressing every key element of responsible aquaculture, including environmental responsibility, social responsibility, food safety, animal welfare, traceability and more. BAP standards encompassing the entire aquaculture production chain, including farms, processing plants, hatcheries and feed mills.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Best Aquaculture Practices 4 Stars
definition: 4 Star BAP accreditation. The BAP program is the world’s most comprehensive third-party certification system for aquaculture facilities, addressing every key element of responsible aquaculture, including environmental responsibility, social responsibility, food safety, animal welfare, traceability and more. BAP standards encompassing the entire aquaculture production chain, including farms, processing plants, hatcheries and feed mills.

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Beter Leven 2 Ster

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Beter leven 3 ster

codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Better Business Bureau Accredited
definition: If a business has been accredited by the BBB, it means BBB has determined that the business meets accreditation standards, which include a commitment to make a good faith effort to resolve any consumer complaints. BBB accredited businesses pay a fee for accreditation review and monitoring for continued compliance and for support of BBB services to the public. BBB Code of Business Practices represents standards for business accreditation by BBB. Businesses based in the United States and Canada that meet these standards and complete all application procedures will be accredited by BBB.  The Code is built on the BBB Standards for Trust, eight principles that summarize important elements of creating and maintaining trust in business.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Better Cotton Initiative
definition: The Better Cotton Initiative (BCI) is a not-for-profit organisation stewarding the global standards for Better Cotton, and bringing together cotton’s complex supply chain, from the farmers to the retailers. BCI exists to make global cotton production better for the people who produce it, better for the environment it grows in and better for the sector’s future, by developing Better Cotton as a sustainable mainstream commodity.

name: Bio-Bayern without Certificate of Provenance
definition:
The biolabel awarded by the Free State of Bavaria offers companies in the farming and food sector in the European Union the opportunity to label goods produced in compliance with the terms of the EU-Eco Regulation in combination with higher quality criteria.
The precisely defined regulations are a guarantee for the consumers of an economic system in harmony with nature and provide them with guidance when making their purchases. Both the farmers of organic products as well as the producers must fulfil the demanding inspection criteria and allow their products to be checked by state-approved and monitored inspection boards. The defined control system ensures a complete traceability of the products over the entire lifecycle. The biolabel awarded by the Free State of Bavaria stands for products and services over and beyond the statutory standards a three-tier control system

name: Bio-LABEL Baden-Württemberg
definition:
The products marked with the Bio-Zeichen Baden-Württemberg are regional organic foods with a traceable origin. The use or labelling is based on the ecological standards of the EC Organic Regulation supplemented with the requirement that the products must be produced in fully converted farms and, in part, on the more stringent requirements of the organic farming associations. The regional origin of the products ensures an additional ecological advantage of the products. The rationality promotes short transport and marketing channels. The independent checks of food by authorized inspection bodies and the additional supervision by the sign holder ensure a high degree of credibility of the sign. The control number printed on the products makes the controls comprehensible.
The seal clearly shows the consumer that the agricultural products and products come from Baden-Württemberg. This ensures not only that the processing takes place in the region, but also that the sourcing of raw materials is 100% regional. In the production and processing of food, the guidelines of the EU Organic Regulation are used as the basis. Many products that are labelled with the Baden-Württemberg organic label are also produced according to the stricter guidelines of an organic farming association. The farms participating in the Bio-Zeichen Baden-Württemberg must be 100% organic. A partial conversion is - with the exception of products from the orchard - not permitted. Neutral controls ensure compliance with the guidelines.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

In 2010, the organic Label - HESSEN was supplemented by another appendix: the European Union logo for organically produced products.
This allows companies to use only one logo on the packaging of their products instead of three different logos, because the European organic label is required.
Behind the Bio-Seal - HESSEN, similar to the quality mark "Tested Quality - HESSEN", there are special requirements for producers, processors and marketers regarding the quality and traceable origin of their products.

The objective of the Biopark label, which has been awarded since 1991, is to promote organic farming. The aim is a closed loop as far as possible. It is about the protection of the environment, landscape management and animal welfare.
Biopark certifies farms that have decided to convert their work to organic farming. The Biopark label can be found on meat and cereal products as well as on potatoes. name: Bleu Blanc Coeur
definition:
The Blue-White-Heart approach was born between 1993 and 2000, from a simple observation made by a dairy farmer, Jean Pierre Pasquet to an agricultural engineer, Pierre Weill. He explained to him that he noticed that in the spring, when his cows were in pasture grass, they were in better shape, and the butter he made was softer and more spreadable than in winter.

From this observation, Jean-Pierre Pasquet and Pierre Weill began their reflection on the importance of preserving the food chain and valuing plants and seeds of nutritional interest. Together, they created an agriculture committed to a sustainable and social approach with breeders eager to feed their fellow citizens.

https://www.awri.com.au/industry_support/entwine/

Because we focus purely on improving the sustainability of tea production – and not herbs, the ETP logo can only be used on products that contain a minimum of 55% Camellia sinensis (tea) by weight.

This process entails a high level of transparency and traceability in their global supply chains. Today, our partner companies range from small, mission-driven coffee roasters to some of the largest transnational corporations in the world.

These can be found on the Producers and Licensees pages respectively.

definition: The FCC is responsible for managing and licensing the electromagnetic spectrum for commercial users and for non-commercial users including: state, county and local governments. This includes public safety, commercial and non-commercial fixed and mobile wireless services, broadcast television and radio, satellite and other services. In licensing the spectrum, the Commission promotes efficient and reliable access to the spectrum for a variety of innovative uses as well as promotes public safety and emergency response.

name: Flamme Verte
definition: Flamme Verte label was launched in France in 2000 by l’Agence de l'Environnement et de la Maîtrise de l'Energie (ADEME), and manufacturers of household appliances. Its mission: to promote the use of wood processing heating appliances of which the design responds to the most demanding quality in terms of fuel efficiency and emissions. In addition, Flamme verte provides assurance that its products are environmentally friendly by emitting very few fine particles.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Flandria
definition: Flandria is the Belgian quality label for fruits and vegetables. It is used by the six most important fruit-and-vegetable auctions grouped under LAVA. Since its inception in 1995, the Flandria label has given added value to fresh products and produce. This seal of approval guarantees concern and care for the environment during their cultivation, plus quality and freshness.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Fleurs de France
definition:
The French agricultural organizations have created a common visual identity in order to highlight the French origin of agricultural products in this case flowers: the signatures "Agricultural Products of France". 

Remarkable to their elegant silhouette in a tricolor pentagon that is available for each family of products, these signatures reflect the commitment of the professionals of the sectors to value the know-how, the territories and the French jobs.

Covering a variety of productions, these signatures all have a common basis, which consists of four criteria:

Origin France of the products concerned,
The existence of specifications or regulations governing the use of the logo,
A formal commitment from the operators of the sectors concerned wishing to use these logos,
Controls performed by a third party.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Monash University FODMAP (Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, and Polyols)
definition: Monash University identified a group of short-chain carbohydrates found in food that are either poorly absorbed in the small intestine or impossible to digest. The Monash team named these carbohydrates FODMAPs, an acronym which stands for Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, and Polyols. This accreditation signifies the product can be used in a low FODMAP diet which can reduce symptoms in people with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). https://www.monashfodmap.com
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: FODMAP (Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, and Polyols) Friendly
definition: The Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, and Polyols (FODMAP) Friendly certification (Fodmap Accreditation) program, incorporating the FODMAP Friendly logo, is the only registered certification trademark worldwide certifying FODMAP levels in food products that have been laboratory tested to be low in FODMAP’s. It is designed to enable consumers with symptoms of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) who are following a Low FODMAP diet to easily identify and select suitable packaged food products.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Food Alliance Certified
definition: Food Alliance Certified attribute includes all products that present a Food Alliance Certified logo.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Food Justice Certified
definition: Food Justice Certified is a label based on high-bar social justice standards for farms, processors, and retailers, including every link in the food chain from farm to table. Our approach is holistic; we ensure fair treatment of workers, fair pricing for farmers, and fair business practices. Food Justice Certified is designed for all agricultural production systems, fiber and cosmetics as well as food.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Food Safety System Certification 22000
definition: The FSSC 22000 Food Safety Management System provides a framework for effectively managing your organization's food safety responsibilities. FSSC 22000 is fully recognized by the Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI) and is based on existing ISO Standards. It demonstrates your company has a robust Food Safety Management System in place that meets the requirements of your customers and consumers. Already, 10.000+ organizations over 140 countries achieved FSSC 22000 certification. With currently 100+ Licensed Certification Bodies and over 1,500 auditors worldwide, our mission is to ensure consumer trust in the supply of safe food and drinks.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Foodland Ontario
definition: Foodland Ontario is a consumer promotion program of the Ontario Ministry of Agriculture and Food. It has partnered with producers to champion, promote and support the consumption of fresh Ontario produce and processed agricultural foods.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: For Life (Social Responsibility)
definition: Demonstration of social and fair business practices; providing good working conditions, guaranteeing the fair treatment of employees and the community and environmental responsibility.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Forest Products - Product Lines From a Certified Forest
definition: At least 70% of the input used to make this product line has been tracked and monitored from its point of origin (a Z809 certified forest) to the end consumer. This mark appears on product and/or packaging. None of the wood-based raw materials shall have come from Controversial Sources.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Forest Stewardship Council 100 Percent
definition:
FSC is a global, not-for-profit organization dedicated to the promotion of responsible forest management worldwide.
The 100% label stands for products containing 100% material from FSC certified forests.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.
