Products with material from FSC certified forests , recycled materials or other controlled sources.

name: Forest Stewardship Council Recycled
definition:
FSC is a global, not-for-profit organization dedicated to the promotion of responsible forest management worldwide.
The label stand for products containing only recycled material.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Foundation ART
definition:
The Foundation ART has the aim to increase the level of anti-theft prevention of two-wheeled vehicles (bicycles, mopeds, scooters and motor cycles). Anti-theft prevention of two-wheeled vehicles can be promoted by influencing social behaviour, registration and tracing, guarded shelters and anti-theft provisions.
The activities of Foundation ART are focussed on (mechanical) anti-theft provisions. The Foundation ART promotes the safety provisions against theft by:
•arranging requirements for mechanical security systems for two-wheeled vehicles
•testing (by third parties) of systems for which an application for homologation was submitted
•certification of approved products
•promoting the use of approved mechanical security systems.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Fran Sverige
definition: In composite products, i.e. a product with at least one added ingredient, at least 75% to be Swedish (water does not count). Bread, cheese and fruit yogurt are examples of composite products. Meat, eggs and raw milk should always be 100% Swedish, even as an ingredient in a product. All animals must be born, raised and slaughtered in Sweden. Cultivation should have taken place in Sweden. All processing and packaging must take place in Sweden.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: France Limousin Meat
definition: France Limousin meat is meat that is constantly monitored from birth to slaughter. Every animal has it's own unique registration number and when exported is assigned an official certificate of origin.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Freiland
definition: The yellow triangle with the flower is only awarded to food and firms that adhere strictly to the principles of organic farming and beyond the highest standards of animal husbandry.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Freshcare
definition: Certification: based on ISO14001. Private non profit owned by Australian horticultural industry bodies. Can certify that a code of practice exists for Viticulture/Winery, only Viticulture or only Winery. Process based and based on ISO14001. Described as a guide how to manage business risk through identification and evaluation. https://www.freshcare.com.au/
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Friend of the Sea
definition:
Friend of the Sea Approved Fisheries:
- target stocks which are not overexploited
- use fishing methods which don't impact the seabed, and
- generate less than average 8% discards.

The French agricultural organizations have created a common visual identity in order to highlight the French origin of agricultural products in this case fruit and legumes: the signatures "Agricultural Products of France".

Remarkable to their elegant silhouette in a tricolor pentagon that is available for each family of products, these signatures reflect the commitment of the professionals of the sectors to value the know-how, the territories and the French jobs.

Covering a variety of productions, these signatures all have a common basis, which consists of four criteria:

Origin France of the products concerned,

name: Ganeden BC30 Probiotic
definition: Ganeden® BC30 (Bacillus coagulans GBI-30, 6086) is a patented probiotic ingredient which can be found in food, beverage, sports nutrition and companion animal products. Unlike most other probiotic strains, Ganeden® BC30 is a spore-former which makes it highly stable and allows it to remain viable through most manufacturing processes, three years of shelf life and the low pH of stomach acid. https://www.ganedenprobiotics.com
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Global Animal Partnership (G.A.P.) 1
definition: Animal Welfare Certified - Base Certification: Base certification is our minimum G.A.P. animal welfare certification level. This means that all of the farms and/or ranches raising the animal have met over 100+ animal welfare standards including more space to move around, and no cages or crates that would confine them. When you see our G.A.P. Animal Welfare Certified label, it means that the animals were raised without antibiotics and no added hormones, and were also fed a vegetarian diet with no animal by-products.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Global Animal Partnership (G.A.P.) 2
definition: Animal Welfare Certified - Enriched Environment: Animals were raised in environments that provide them with more space and additional enrichments (such as straw bales and perches) to encourage natural behaviors. Again, all G.A.P. certified animals were raised without antibiotics or any added hormones, and were fed a vegetarian diet with no animal by-products.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Global Animal Partnership (G.A.P.) 3
definition: Animal Welfare Certified - Outdoor Access: Animals have the choice of indoor or outdoor living (weather permitting for poultry), and also have additional enrichments indoors and out. At this level, farms and ranches ensure the animals are managed in both environments.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Global Animal Partnership (G.A.P.) 4
definition: Animal Welfare Certified - Pasture Raised: Animals are raised on pasture year-round. In some climates where pastures need to be protected for use the next year, animals must still be given daily access to outdoor areas. Cattle, sheep, goats and bison are not permitted to be finished in feedlots. Farmers and ranchers raise animals that are well suited for outdoor living, and sustainably manage their environments.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Global Animal Partnership (G.A.P.) 5
definition: Animal Welfare Certified - Animal Centered: Animals live on pasture year-round, with protection from the environment (shelters, windbreak, etc.). Farmers and ranchers raise animals that are well suited for outdoor living, and sustainably manage their environments. No physical alterations are performed on any of the animals (e.g. castration, tail docking, etc).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Global Animal Partnership (G.A.P.) 5 Plus
definition: Animal Welfare Certified - Entire Life on Farm: This is our top tier of animal welfare certification. All of the requirements of the Animal Centered level are met (animals live on pasture year round with protection, no physical alterations allowed, etc.) but animals are also processed on-farm, or through the use of a mobile slaughter facility, so their entire life is spent on the farm.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Gaskeur
definition: Gaskeur is a hallmark of KIWA. The label is applied voluntarily in the Netherlands to boilers. It indicates the additional standards the installation complies with, above the legal requirements that the equipment must meet. It is an addition to the CE mark.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: GASTEC QA
definition: GASTEC QA (Quality Approved) is a quality mark for gas related products and is issued exclusively by KIWA. GASTEC QA not only makes the quality and safety of the product itself visible but also of the whole production process.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: GCP – Global Coffee Platform
definition: The GCP logo is the key identifier of the Global Coffee Platform. It symbolizes the core attributes that are at the heart of what the organization does: farmer-centric, multi-stakeholder, inclusive, shared responsibility.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Origine France Garantie

The Origine France Garantie certification was created in June 2010 following the publication of Yves Jégo's report on the France brand.

The certification, simple and understandable by all, is the result of a collective approach of actors who wish to work together to promote the "produce in France" and the valorization of industrial and artisan know-how.

The Pro France association which promotes Origine France Garantie is made up of business leaders supporting this initiative. Its goal is:

Give clear and precise information to the consumer about the French origin of the products
Make known the companies that manufacture in France
The Origine France Garantie certification distinguishes itself from other mentions such as "made in France", "designed in France", "Made in France" ... which are self-declarative and too loose.

Origine France Garantie is the only certification that certifies the French origin of a product. It is transversal (all sectors combined) and indisputable (certification, mandatory, is carried out by an independent certifying body).

The Origine France Garantie certification ensures consumers traceability of the product by giving a clear and objective indication of origin.

Certification is achieved through two cumulative criteria that companies must meet to obtain it:

Between 50% and 100% of the unit cost is French
The product takes its essential characteristics in France

Pro-Cert provides professional organic certification services to the following Standards/Regulations:

2.Equivalency to the European Organic Program
3.The USDA National Organic Program (NOP)
4.The Quebec Organic Program (CARTV)
5.Japanese Agricultural Standard (JAS via CERES)

name: Produit en Bretagne

Originally designed to indicate the Breton origin of the product, the logo displays it in letters. This is how the current logo was born, on a corner of paper tablecloth.

This sketch was brought back to Brittany and acclaimed by the members of the time.

After two years of tests in stores, and a very favourable reception from Scarmor stores (E. Leclerc stores), the logo is adopted and the statutes are fixed in 1995.

SKG is an independent organisation that monitors the quality of products in the construction industry. On the basis of an inspection SKG determines how much resistance a lock or latch provides against burglary. This resistance is in 3 classes.
1 Star - 3 minutes (standard burglar proof)
Building hardware with this label means that it provides at least 3 minutes resistance to burglary with simple tools like a crowbar or screwdriver.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

2 Stars - 3 minutes (heavily burglar-proof): With security locks and latches this label must provide for at least 3 minutes resistance to burglary with a comprehensive tool kit.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: SKG 3 star
definition:
SKG is an independent organisation that monitors the quality of products in the construction industry. On the basis of an inspection SKG determines how much resistance a lock or latch provides against burglary. This resistance is in 3 classes.
3 Stars - 5 minutes (extra heavy anti-burglary): Building hardware with this label have to provide resistance to a burglar with heavy tools for at least 5 minutes for your property. It is not only the lock, the hinges and the cylinder that has to be of this heavy quality, but also the door and the frame must provide sufficient resistance.

The label certifies that the guidelines of Verbund Ökohöfe e.V. are met. These guidelines are stronger than the legal requirements of the EU for organic farming (EC-Eco-Basis Ordinance (EC) No. 834/2007). 
For example, the following rules apply to the producers: 
- In cattle keeping: no dehorning, no tethering, pasture (at least 100 days) 
- CMS hybrids from protoplast fusion (horticultural cultures) and rye, wheat, triticale, barley, flower and herbal hybrids are not permitted. In addition, different restrictions apply to vegetable hybrids. - Conventional dung GMO (genetically modified organism) fed mammals is not permitted.
- Copper preparations may only be used in fruit, wine and potato cultivation (maximum copper quantity 3kg / ha and year, calculated on the basis of the five-year average of rotation). 
- For horticultural crops, a 100 m distance to the motorway and 30 m to other busy roads must be observed.
- settlecomposts - also from quality-tested systems - are not permissible, since the GMO is not guaranteed in the process.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

Covering a variety of productions, these signatures all have a common basis, which consists of four criteria:

Origin France of the products concerned,
The existence of specifications or regulations governing the use of the logo,
A formal commitment from the operators of the sectors concerned wishing to use these logos,
Controls performed by a third party.

name: Viande Chevaline Francaise
definition:
The French agricultural organizations have created a common visual identity in order to highlight the French origin of agricultural products in this case chevaline products: the signatures "Agricultural Products of France". 
Remarkable to their elegant silhouette in a tricolor pentagon that is available for each family of products, these signatures reflect the commitment of the professionals of the sectors to value the know-how, the territories and the French jobs.  Covering a variety of productions, these signatures all have a common basis, which consists of four criteria:
Origin France of the products concerned,
The existence of specifications or regulations governing the use of the logo,
A formal commitment from the operators of the sectors concerned wishing to use these logos,
Controls performed by a third party.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Vignerons en Développement Durable (VDD)
definition: Certification: Based on ISO26000 (social responsibility). Private, France - Started with a charter created by 10 producers in 2007, and is still producer run. The charter has 37 commitments. The cellars create their own specific performance goals which must be met. The individual performance goals are to be used as a framework for decision making. v-dd.com
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Vím, co jím
definition: The logo marks quality foodstuffs that are nutritionally balanced. Food and beverages products marked with logo “Vím, co jím” contain less salt, added sugars, trans-fatty acids and saturated fatty acids. For some product categories, it informs the consumer that the product is rich of fiber and/or contain appropriate amount of energy (calories). The same logo is used in both the Czech Republic (under the name “Vím, co jím”) and Slovakia (under the name “Viem, čo jem”). This program is part of the global program “The Choices Programme”. https://www.vimcojim.cz
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Vinatura
definition: Swiss wine out of sustainable production.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Product of the Vinho Verde Region
definition: The Seal of Guarantee certifies the authenticity and genuineness of Vinho Verde, assuring its origin and strict controls carried out at all stages of the production process, from the vineyard to the glass. Each stamp is unique, with coding both unique and traceable.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Viticulture Durable en Champagne (VDC)
definition: Certification: Viticulture Durable en Champagne. Regional, Champagne, France. French wine region with own certification. Similar to national HVE. Champagne as a region has recognised the need to go from being the least sustainable wine region in France to the most - especially as it is vulnerable to global warming, image effects and quality questions of bulk grape purchases. https://www.champagne.fr/en/viticulture-durable/
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: V.I.V.A.
definition: Certification: Equalitas does not consider VIVA to be a certification but a “declaration” of data results. National, governmental, Italy. First sustainability certification of wine to be directly promoted by a national government. http://www.viticolturasostenibile.org/EN
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Warrant holder of the court of Belgium
definition: Becoming an official supplier to the Belgian Court is a source of particular pride for a craftsman or company to seeing their talent and professionalism rightly recognized by His Majesty the King.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Weidemelk
definition: A certification given in the Netherlands to dairy products made from milk produced by cattle (bovine) that is allowed to roam free in the pasture for at least a minimum of 120 days in a year.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Weight Watchers Endorsed
definition: Foods and meals in the Weight Watchers program are assigned points, and you're allotted a certain number of points daily depending on your initial body weight and weight loss goals. Some packaged food brands and even certain restaurants have teamed up with Weight Watchers to promote this healthy point-based weight-loss program.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Welfare Quality
definition: Welfare Quality states that the welfare of the animals both on the farm and during slaughter is followed in accordance with the welfare quality procedure. Consumers know that the welfare of the animals is protected.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Kosher Western Kosher (WK)
definition:
Western Kosher provides assistance with Kashruth supervision by certifying bakeries, butcher shops, caterers, restaurants, hotels, manufacturers or processors involved in producing Kosher food products for year-round use for Canada and the United States. 

Western Kosher, formerly the Vaad Ha'ir of Winnipeg, provides its 120 licensees with the North American standard of kashruth – a standard adhered to throughout all of Canada and the U.S.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Whole Grain 100 Percent Stamp
definition: The Whole Grain 100 Percent Stamp is a program of The Whole Grain Council. The Whole Grains Council helps consumers find whole grain foods and understand their health benefits; helps manufacturers and restaurants create delicious whole grain foods; and helps the media write accurate, compelling stories about whole grains. If a product bears the 100% Stamp, then all its grain ingredients are whole grains. There is a minimum requirement of 16g (16 grams) – a full serving – of whole grain per labelled serving, for products using the 100% Stamp.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Whole Grain Basic Stamp
definition: The Whole Grain Basic Stamp is a program of The Whole Grain Council. The Whole Grains Council helps consumers find whole grain foods and understand their health benefits; helps manufacturers and restaurants create delicious whole grain foods; and helps the media write accurate, compelling stories about whole grains. If a product bears the Basic Stamp, it contains at least 8g (8 grams) – a half serving – of whole grain, but may also contain some refined grain. Even if a product contains large amounts of whole grain (23g, 37g, 41g, etc.), it will use the Basic Stamp if it also contains extra bran, germ, or refined flour.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Whole Grain Council Stamp
definition: The Whole Grain Stamp is a certification symbol from the Oldways Whole Grains Council that communicates the gram amount of whole grain in a product. There are three different versions of the Whole Grain Stamp that can appear on packages (the 100% Stamp, the 50%+ Stamp, and the Basic Stamp), depending on what percentage of the grain ingredients are whole grain (or in Canada, what percentage of the product weight is whole grain).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Whole grains 50 percent Stamp
definition: If a product bears the 50%+ Stamp, then at least half of its grain ingredients are whole grain. There is a minimum requirement of 8 grams– a half serving – of whole grain per labelled serving, for products using the 50%+ Stamp.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: WIETA (Wine and Agricultural Ethical Trading Association)
definition: The Wine and Agricultural Ethical Trading Association (WIETA). WIETA’s vision is to promote fair treatment, respectful relationships and dignified lives toward achieving a transformed agricultural sector.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Sustainable wineries for climate protection
definition:
The Sustainable Wineries for Climate Protection (SWfCP) certification, developed by the Spanish Wine Federation (FEV), is aimed at the continuous improvement and sustainability of wineries, acting on four fundamental pillars: Environmental, Social, Economic and Governance to align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Note: it’s the evolution of the sustainability seal, "Wineries for Climate Protection ’, which was created in 2015.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Kosher Supervisors of Wisconsin Certification
definition: Kosher Supervisors of Wisconsin Certification
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Water Quality Association (WQA's)- Tested and Certified
definition: WQA's Certified Product Listings are available to help connect consumers with water treatment products that have been tested and certified to industry standards. WQA's Gold Seal Product Certification Program ensures that the product is constructed or formulated from safe materials, the claims listed on the packaging are backed by test data, and the product will hold up under normal usage conditions.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: WSDA
definition: Washington State Department of Agriculture Organic Food Program, Washington State Department of Agriculture Organic Food Program (WSDA) Organic Food Program  The WSDA Organic Food Program, a USDA-accredited certifier, upholds the integrity of the organic label through certification and inspection of organic crop and livestock producers, processors, handlers and retailers. Whether you are looking to market your organic product at home or abroad, WSDA offers certification services to meet your needs. Please browse below to find out how WSDA can put your business on the path to certification.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: WWF Panda
definition: Products that support the WWF http://www.worldwildlife.org/
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Zeldzaam Lekker
definition: This label is awarded to companies that support (through their products or services) the preservation of rare or uncommon cattle and animal sorts.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Zero Waste Business Council Certified
definition: U.S. Zero Waste Business Council Certification Program is created by U.S. Zero Waste Business Council. It is the first third-party Zero Waste Facility Certification program for facilities that meet the requests of Zero Waste Business for a valid, comprehensive verification of their Zero Waste achievements.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Front of Package
definition: The front of package nutrient label displays important nutrition information from the nutrition facts panel (found on the back and sides of packages) in a clear, simple and easy-to-use format on the front of food and beverage packages.  This subset of the nutrition information will assist the consumer in their purchasing decisions by highlighting specific nutrients.
codeListDefinition: Indication of which nutrition call outs or highlights are on the package. A nutrition call out is a graphic which highlights some elements from the nutrition panel for the consumer to have a quick view for example, Front of Package information.

name: Chemically Hardened
definition: The material has been treated to have additional resistance to deformation or change.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Compressed
definition: The material has been subjected to compressive stress which results in reduction of volume as compared to an uncompressed but otherwise identical state.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Injection Moulded
definition: The material was manufactured by injection moulding, which consists of feeding the material into a heated barrel, mixed, and forced into a mold cavity where it cools and hardens to the configuration of the cavity.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Insulated
definition: The material has been designed or processed to reduce heat transfer.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Moisture Resistant
definition: The material property that resists uptake or passage of water. The resistance of a packaging material to deterioration or change when in contact with water. To be water resistant is not to be waterproof.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Moulded
definition: The material was manufactured by moulding, which consists of filling a mold with the material on liquid form and allowing it to harden so it takes the shape of the mold.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Vacuum Formed
definition: A process through which a material is heated to a forming temperature, stretched onto or into a single-surface mould, and held against the mould by applying a vacuum between the mould surface and the sheet.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Water Repellent
definition: The material has been treated or processed so it can resist the ingress of water under specified conditions
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Base to stand up vertically
definition: A general term applied to the support or pedestal of an object.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bung seal
definition: A bung is an apparatus used to seal a container, such as a bottle, barrel or tube. A bung is partially inserted inside the container to act as a seal.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cage/Muzzle
definition: A cage that fits over the cork of a bottle of champagne, sparkling wine or beer to prevent the cork from emerging under the pressure of the carbonated contents.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cap
definition: A cap that seals a bottle or other form of packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Carrier
definition: A device of various types attached to or hang from trolleys to support the load.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Consumption utensil
definition: An item which allows the user to extract and/or consume the content of a container or product (straws, spoons, ice cream stick).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cork
definition: A small cylinder that is pushed into the packaging to close it.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Coupler
definition: A device for connecting parts of barrel, cask etc.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Divider/Protector
definition: A component in packaging to serve as protecting the product and/or also the packaging shape.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Edge protection
definition: A right-angle piece placed over the outermost perimeter edges of a container to distribute pressure and prevent collapse or cutting from banding, strapping, or handling.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Flap
definition: A piece of material, hinged or attached only on one side, that covers an opening or hangs down from the packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Handle
definition: A grip attached to an object for using or moving the object, usually with the hands.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Label
definition: A label is a piece of paper, polymer, cloth, metal, or other material affixed to a container or article (or printed directly upon it), which usually carries information about the article to which it has been attached.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Lid
definition: In packaging, the top or bottom of a container, usually the part that closes the opening; may also be known as cap, over, or top.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Liner
definition: An internal chamber within a container which separates the content of the container from the walls. Inner liners provide additional isolation and protection to the content of a container. Sometimes coatings of certain materials may be applied as an alternative to inner liners.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Lightning stopper swing-top (LSST)
definition: The LSST is a pin with a spring and a toggle lever principle, usually made of porcelain or plastic, with a sealing ring, mainly for closing bottles. Opening and closing can be done by hand as often as desired and does not require any aid such as a bottle opener. Also known as a flip-top.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Main package type
definition: The code to designate the material that pertains to the value defined in packageTypeCode.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Peg
definition: A fastener which allows a product to be hanged.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Sleeve
definition: A tubular form, open at both ends, that is slipped over an item or package.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Spigot
definition: A small peg, plug or tapl, especially for insertion into the vent of a cask.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Tab
definition: A flexible cover which can be easily removed in order to open a container.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Tag
definition: A hanging card made of any material which is used to identify or provide additional information of a product.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Tap
definition: A device that controls the flow of liquid/gas.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: First Submission of Packaging
definition: First submission of packaging (use for new trade items or existing trade items without packaging changes.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Similar or Equa to Current Packaging
definition: Similar or equal to current packaging (use if there is no change to the performance of the packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Improved Packaging Performance
definition: Improved packaging performance (use if the new packaging improves the performance than the previous packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Reduced Packaging Performance
definition: Reduced packaging performance (use if the new packaging reduces the performance than the previous packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bamboo
definition: Any of various woody or arborescent grasses (as of the genera Bambusa, Arundinaria, and Dendrocalamus of the subfamily Bambusoideae) of tropical and temperate regions having hollow stems, thick rhizomes, and shoots. The packaging may be in the form of paper, wood or leaves.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cellulose hydrate
definition: A class of materials manufactured by the conversion of natural cellulose to a soluble cellulosic derivative and subsequent regeneration, typically forming a film (e.g., cellophane).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Ceramic
definition: A non-specific material made from clay and hardened by firing at a high temperatures. Examples can include Terra-cotta, Earthenware, Stoneware, Porcelain, and High-Tech Ceramics.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cloth or Fabric
definition: A non specific material made by weaving, felting, knitting, or crocheting natural and/or synthetic fibers.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite
definition: A material that is made from multiple materials.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Natural cork
definition: Cork is an impermeable buoyant material, the phellem layer of bark tissue that is harvested for commercial use primarily from Quercus suber (the cork oak).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Double Wall Corrugated Board
definition: A structure formed by five layers of cardboard: two fluted sheets and three linerboards (two outer liners and one intermediate liner). Also known as 5-layer type.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Corrugated Board Other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of corrugated boards. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Single Wall Corrugated Board
definition: A structure formed by three layers of cardboard: one fluted sheet and two outer linerboards. Also known as 3-layer type or double faced.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Triple Wall Corrugated Board
definition: A structure formed by seven layers of cardboard: three fluted sheets and four linerboards (two outer liners and two intermediate liners). Also known as 7-layer type.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Fibre Burlap
definition: The American name for cloth woven from jute plant skins and other vegetable fibres. In other parts of the world it is known as Hessian, Hessian cloth, or gunny from the Indian gain.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cotton
definition: A natural cellulosic seed-hair fiber, obtained from the seed pod of the cotton plant. First known in India about 3000 B.C.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Flax
definition: The plant from the stem of which bast fiber is extracted by retting to produce linen. An erroneous term for linen fiber, particularly in blends.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Hemp
definition: Hemp is a commonly used term for varieties of the Cannabis plant. Hemp can yield fibre which can be used in ropes, cloths, weaves, as a reinforcement of polymer composites as well as pulps for paper making.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Jute
definition: A bast fiber obtained from the round pod jute or the long pod jute of the family Tiliaceae. Jute ribbon is purely made from the jute plant. Grown extensively in Pakistan and India, mainly in the Bengal district of Pakistan.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Fibre Other
definition: A non specific material made of a unit of matter, either natural or manufactured, that forms the basic element of fabrics and other textile structures.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Solidified Foam
definition: A non specific material in a lightweight cellular form resulting from introduction of gas bubbles during manufacture, used to reduce shock and vibration or abrasion.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Glass
definition: A substance mainly consisting of sand, lime and soda, fused at high temperatures and cooled quickly so that it solidifies to a vitreous or noncrystalline condition. This term applies to transparent clear glass or as a generic term if distinction with coloured glass is not desired. Example: sodocalcite.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Coloured Glass
definition: Glass containing external colouring or glass that has been coloured by the addition of colouring agents/particles in its creation
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Laminated Carton
definition: A material made up of laminates of paperboard, foil and polyethylene which combined form a sheet suitable for asceptic processing.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Aluminum
definition: A non specific material made from aluminum or aluminum alloy.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Brass
definition: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Metal Composite
definition:
Refers to an object that is composed of two separate metals joined together. 
Instead of being a mixture of two or more metals, like alloys, metal composites consist of layers of different metals.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Iron
definition: A heavy metallic element (Fe) capable of being fashioned into a variety of forms.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Lead
definition: A bluish-white soft malleable ductile plastic but inelastic heavy metallic element (Pb)
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Metal other
definition: A non specific material made from metal or metal alloy material.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Stainless Steel
definition: An alloy of steel with chromium and sometimes another element (as nickel or molybdenum) that is practically immune to rusting and ordinary corrosion
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Steel
definition: Commercial iron that contains carbon in any amount up to about 1.7 percent as an essential alloying constituent, is malleable when under suitable conditions, and is distinguished from cast iron by its malleability and lower carbon content.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Tin
definition: Tin is a chemical element that is obtained chiefly from the mineral cassiterite, where it occurs as an oxide, SnO2. This silvery, malleable poor metal is not easily oxidized in air, and is used to coat other metals to prevent corrosion. It is used in many alloys, most notably bronze
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Calcium Carbonate
definition: Ground calcium carbonate and precipitated calcium carbonate products serve as functional fillers in plastic and rubber applications. Calcium carbonate is widely used as in polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyolefin, polypropylene (PP), polyethylene (PE) and unsaturated polyester resins applications.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Mineral Other
definition: Any other mineral-based material not available in this list.  Should be used as a temporary measure while a proper code is established
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Talc
definition: Talc is used to stiffen thermoplastics, mainly polypropylene but also polyethylene and polyamide (Nylon).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Natural rubber
definition: A strong elastic material made by drying the sap from various tropical trees, especially the American rubber tree.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Corrugated Paper
definition: Heavy paper with ridges and grooves, used in packing fragile articles.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Kraft paper
definition: Kraft paper is the paper grade with the highest strength. It is used for the production of e.g. paper bags, emery paper or shopping bags.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Kraft paper (wet strength)
definition: The wet-strength kraft paper has a certain tear strength when wet due to special additives. It is used for the production of e.g. paper bags, emery paper or shopping bags.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Molded Pulp
definition: Used for producing pulp-based or fibrous products by pressing; example products: egg packages, trays and boxes for fruits and vegetables.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Paper Other
definition: Any other paper-based material not available in this list.  Should be used as a temporary measure while a proper code is established.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Paper
definition: A non-specific sheet material produced by the matting of fibres from wood, rags, or other fibrous materials.  Generally, paper is of a lesser thickness or weight than paperboard.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Paperboard
definition: A non specific material, generally made from cotton or wood, that describe a variety or of board materials used in the production of boxes, folding cartons, and solid fibre and corrugated shipping containers; also termed cardboard
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Rayon Paper
definition: Generic term for a manmade fiber derived from regenerated cellulose.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Plant Leaves
definition: Plant leaves, such as banana leaves, including wet or dry leaves. In some cases, leaves are pre-softened by steaming.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bioplastic
definition: Plastic materials made from biomass, but may have exactly the same properties as ordinary plastic. Sometimes these plastics are biodegradable.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Plastic Other
definition: A non-specific material made of any of numerous organic synthetic or processed materials that are mostly thermoplastic or thermosetting polymers of high molecular weight and that can be made into objects, films, or filaments.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Thermoplastics
definition: A non-specific substance that becomes soft and pliable when heated, without a change in its intrinsic properties. Polystyrene and polyethylene are thermoplastics.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyethylene Terephthalate, amorphous (APET)
definition: Polyethylene Terephthalate, amorphous (APET) has a very high transparency, is flame retardant and suitable for direct food contact. It is used for packaging of all kinds.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polypropylene, longitudinally and laterally stretched (BOPP)
definition: Biaxially oriented PP (BOPP) films are characterized by their tear, impact and puncture resistance. The film is mainly used in food packaging, e.g. as candy wrap or wrapping for chocolate bars.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cellulose Acetate
definition: Cellulose acetate is one of the most important esters of cellulose. Depending on the way it has been processed cellulose acetate can be used for a wide variety of applications, e.g. films, membranes or fibers.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Crystallized polyethylene terephthalate (CPET)
definition: Crystallized polyethylene terephthalate (CPET) is a variation of standard PET which has been crystallized for heat resistance, rigidity, and toughness
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Epoxy
definition: Epoxy resins are thermoset polymers which are frequently used as coatings for metal packaging such as soft-drink cans.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Expanded polystyrene (EPS)
definition: Expanded polystyrene is a rigid, tough, closed cell and lightweight thermoplastic foam material. It is manufactured by expanding spherical beads in a mold, using heat and pressure to fuse the beads together. While each individual bead is a closed cell environment, there are significant open spaces between each bead.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Ethylene vinyl acetate, (EVA)
definition: Ethylene vinyl acetate, a copolymer of 60 to 90% ethylene and 40 to 10% vinyl acetate.  Packaging applications include soft films, coatings, hot melt adhesives, wine cork substitutes, and closure seals for plastic and metal container caps.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Ethylene vinyl alcohol, (EVOH)
definition: Ethylene vinyl alcohol, a copolymer of ethylene and vinyl alcohol. A plastic resin commonly used in food applications to provide barrier to oxygen and other gases.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: High Density Polyethylene (HDPE)
definition: High-Density PolyEthylene (HDPE) is a polyethylene thermoplastic made from petroleum.  A strong, relatively opaque form of polyethylene having a dense structure with few side branches off the main carbon backbone. Can be applied to bottles, flasks and caps.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE)
definition: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is a polyethylene thermoplastic made from petroleum.  A strong form of polyethylene having a less dense structure with more side branches off the main carbon backbone (on about 2% of the carbon atoms) than HDPE; therefore its tensile strength is lower, and its resilience is higherMade in translucent or opaque variations, it is quite flexible, and tough to the degree of being almost unbreakable.  It is widely used for manufacturing various containers, dispensing bottles, wash bottles, tubing, plastic bags for computer components, and various moulded laboratory equipment. Its most common use is in plastic bags.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Linear Low Density Polyethylene
definition: Linear low density polyethylene is a linear polyethylene with a significant number of short branches on the polymer backbone. It is commonly made by copolymerization of ethylene with longer-chain olefins. It is different from LDPE due to the absence of long chain branches which gives it higher tensile strength, impact and puncture resistance than LDPE. Common uses of LLDPE are plastic bags, wraps, stretch wraps, pouches, covers and lids.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Medium-density Polyethylene
definition: Medium-density polyethylene is a type of polyethylene defined by a density range of 0.926-0.940 g/cm3. MDPE is typically used in shrink films, sacks, packaging film and carrier bags.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Nylon
definition: Packaging applications include oven-baking bags (nylon 6 and nylon 66) and barrier layers (MXD6 and nylon 6) for PET and HDPE bottles. Very occasionally, bottles can be made of nylon.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Oriented polypropylene (OPP)
definition: Oriented polypropylene (OPP) is made of a soft polypropylene material which is stretched in a transverse or longitudinal direction (monoaxial) and becomes therefore brittle. Also known as: biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP), CAS Registry Number: 9003-07-0
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polymers Other
definition: A non-specific chemical compound or mixture of compounds formed by polymerization and consisting essentially of repeating structural units
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyamide (PA)
definition: A polymer with repeating units linked by amide bonds. Polyamides (PA) occur both naturally and artificially, examples of naturally occurring polyamides are proteins, such as wool and silk. Artificially made polyamides can be  nylons, aramids, and sodium poly(aspartate).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyacrylonitril (PAN)
definition: Polyacrylonitril is a organic polymer which is frequently used in fibres for textiles. As fibres the material is frequently referred to as Acrylic.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polycarbonate (PC)
definition: Polycarbonate, a transparent thermoplastic which is used in a wide variety of applications including CDs and DVDs, eyeglasses, cell phone covers, laptops as well as packaging applications such as bottles.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polycaprolactone (PCL)
definition: Polycaprolactone is a biodegradable polyester which is also used in in the manufacturing of polyurethanes. It is also used in blends with thermoplastic starch to improve properties and can also be used as a plasticizer to PVC.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyethylene (PE)
definition: A thermoplastic composed of the polymers of ethylene.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyethylene Naphthalate (PEN)
definition: Polyethylene naphthalate is a polymer with good barrier properties (unlike Polyethylene terephthalate). It is well-suited for production of the amber-colored bottles meant for packing beverages like beer.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)
definition: Polyethylene terephthalate is a thermoplastic polymer resin of the polyester family and is used in synthetic fibers. Can be applied to bottles, flasks and caps.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol (PETG)
definition: Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol (PETG) is a PET modified with glycol, which is characterized by its aqueous properties (viscosity). Applications are found in injection molding.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA)
definition: Polyhydroxyalkanoates are linear polyesters produced in nature by bacterial fermentation of sugar or lipids.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polylactic Acid or Polylactide (PLA)
definition: Polylactic acid or Polylactide is a biodegradable, thermoplastic, aliphatic polyester derived from lactic acid.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA)
definition: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA) is often used as a lightweight and shatterproof alternative to glass, due to its transparency, brilliance and scratch resistance, PMMA is therefore often referred to as acrylic glass.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyoxymethylene (POM)
definition: Polyoxymethylene (POM) is a thermoplastic with good mechanical properties and high dimensional stability. Fields of application are the automotive industry and electrical engineering, in packaging it is used for e.g. spray cans, gas lighter tanks, gas ampoules. Also known as acetal, polyacetal, and polyformaldehyde.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polypropylene (PP)
definition: A non-specific material made of various thermoplastic plastics or fibers that are polymers of propylene.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polystyrene (PS)
definition: A polymer prepared by the polymerization of styrene as the sole monomer
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyurethanes (PU)
definition: Polyurethanes are primarily thermoset resins which are used in the manufacture of flexible and rigid foams, microcellular foam seals and gaskets, as well as high performance adhesives, surface coatings and sealants. Polyurethane can also be used to make synthetic fibers.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyvinyl Alcohol (PVA)
definition: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA or PVOH) is a biodegradable and highly water soluble polymer with high gas and grease barrier. Common uses for PVA are paper adhesives, paper coatings, as a self-standing water soluble films as well as blends to improve processability of thermoplastic starch.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC)
definition: A polymer of vinyl chloride used especially for electrical insulation, films, and pipes
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyvinylidene Chloride (PVDC)
definition: Polyvinylidene chloride is primarily used as a barrier coating to provide barrier against fat, vapour and gases.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Styrene acrylonitrile (SAN)
definition: Styrene acrylonitrile (SAN) is a copolymer transparent and rigid plastic. Examples of applications are kitchenware and cosmetic packaging.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Thermoplastic Starch (TPS)
definition: Thermoplastic starch is obtained through destructurization of natural starch through exposure to shear and heat. TPS is most frequently used in blends with biodegradable synthetic polymers such as PCL and PVA.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Extruded polystyrene (XPS)
definition: Extruded polystyrene is a rigid, tough, closed cell and lightweight thermoplastic foam material. It is manufactured using a process of extrusion that produces a homogeneous "closed cell" matrix with each cell fully enclosed by polystyrene walls.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Rubber
definition: A strong elastic synthetic substance made either by improving the qualities of natural rubber or by an industrial process using petroleum and coal products
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Vinyl
definition: A non-specific polymer of a vinyl compound or a product (as a resin or a textile fiber) made from such a polymer
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Hardboard
definition: Hardboard (not to be confused with hardwood), also called High-Density Fiberboard (HDF), is a type of fiberboard, which is similar to particle board and medium-density fiberboard, but is denser, much stronger and harder because it is made out of exploded wood fibers which have been highly compressed. Consequently, the density of hardboard is 31 lbs or more per cubic foot (500 kg/m³)[2] and is usually about 50-65 lbs per cubic foot (800–1040 kg/m³). It differs from particle board in that the bonding of the wood fibers requires no additional materials, although resin is often added. Unlike particle board, it will not split or crack.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Hardwood
definition: A general term referring to any variety of broad-leaved, deciduous trees, and the wood from those trees. The term has nothing to do with the actual hardness of the wood; some hardwoods are softer than certain softwood (evergreen) species.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Medium density fibreboard
definition: Medium-Density Fibreboard (MDF) is an engineered wood product made by breaking down hardwood or softwood residuals into wood fibres, combining them with wax and a resin binder, and forming panels by applying high temperature and pressure. MDF is generally denser than plywood. It is made up of separated fibres, but can be used as a building material similar in application to plywood. It is stronger and much more dense than particle board.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Oriented strand board (OSB)
definition: Oriented Strand Board (OSB), also known as sterling board, sterling OSB, aspenite, and smartply, is an engineered wood particle board formed by adding adhesives and then compressing layers of wood strands (flakes) in specific orientations. OSB may have a rough and variegated surface with the individual strips of around 2.5 × 15 cm (1" × 6"), lying unevenly across each other and comes in a variety of types.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Wood other
definition: A non specific material made from the hard fibrous lignified substance under the bark of trees.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Particle board
definition: Particle Board, also known as particleboard, chipboard, and Low-Density Fiberboard (LDF), is an engineered wood product manufactured from wood chips, sawmill shavings, or sawdust, and a synthetic resin or other suitable binder, which is pressed and extruded. Particle board is a composite material.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Plywood
definition: Plywood, a manufactured wood panel similar to LDF, MDF, and HDF, is made from layering thin sheets of wood. Plywood layers (called veneers or plies) are glued together, with adjacent plies having their wood grain rotated relative to adjacent layers up to 90 degrees.  All plywoods bind resin and wood fibre sheets (cellulose cells are long, strong and thin) to form a composite material.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Softwood
definition: General term used to describe lumber produced from needle and/or cone bearing trees (Conifers).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bio-based polymer
definition: The packaging material is made from bio-based polymers whole or partially from renewable biological resources, like sugar cane, starch.
codeListDefinition: A code describing the type of raw or recycled material the packaging material is made from.

name: Crude Oil
definition: The packaging material is made from crude oil.
codeListDefinition: A code describing the type of raw or recycled material the packaging material is made from.

name: Virgin/new raw material other
definition: The packaging material is made from virgin, non-recycled raw materials, such as aluminium or wood.
codeListDefinition: A code describing the type of raw or recycled material the packaging material is made from.

name: Recycled
definition: The packaging material is made from post consumer recycled content.
codeListDefinition: A code describing the type of raw or recycled material the packaging material is made from.

name: Composting Organic Recovery
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Energy Recovery
definition: To allow optimization of energy recovery in a real industry system, the theoretical calorific gain shall be well above zero. To claim energy recovery qnet shall be equal to greater than qnet,min,real as defined for various incineration conditions.  Reference ISO18605:2013(E) Annex A.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Material Recycling
definition: The supplier shall be able to demonstrate that the procedures defined in normative ISO 18604:2013(E) Annexes A and ISO 18604:2013(E) B have been followed in arriving at the final design of the finish
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Other
definition: Code value not available in code list.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Deutscher Mindeststandard
definition: The German minimum standard for determining the recyclability of packaging, subject to system packaging pursuant to section 21 (3) VerpackG (Verpackungsgesetz–Packaging Act).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Other
definition: Code value not available in code list.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Post-consumer Recycled Content
definition: The ratio of post-consumer recycled material (post-consumer and pre consumer as defined by ISO 14021) to total material used in packaging constituents, packaging components, or packaging systems.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Pre-consumer Recycled Content
definition: The ratio of pre-consumer recycled material (post-consumer and pre consumer as defined by ISO 14021) to total material used in packaging constituents, packaging components, or packaging systems
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Compostable
definition: Packaging that can biodegrade generating a relatively homogeneous and stable humus-like substance.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Energy Recoverable
definition: Packaging which allows for a net calorific gain in energy recovery operations.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Recyclable
definition: Packaging material and format which can be diverted from the waste stream through available processes and programmes and can be collected, processed and returned to use in the form of raw materials or products.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Reusable
definition: Packaging that has been conceived and designed to accomplished within its life cycle a certain number of trips, rotations or uses for the same purpose for which it was conceived.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyethylene Terephthalates
definition: Recycling scheme code 1 relates to Polyethylene terephthalates.  These recyclables represent polyester fibres' (Polar Fleece), thermoformed sheet, strapping, soft drink bottles, tote bags, furniture, carpet, panelling and (occasionally) new containers which can be picked up through most curb side recycling programs.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: High-density Polyethylenes
definition: Recycling scheme code 2 relates to High-density polyethylenes.  These recyclables represent bottles, grocery bags, milk jugs, recycling bins, agricultural pipe, base cups, car stops, playground equipment, and plastic lumber which can be picked up through most curb side recycling programs, although some allow only those containers with necks.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Corrugated fibreboard (cardboard)
definition: Recycling scheme code 20 relates to corrugated fibreboard (cardboard).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Mixed paper/Non-corrugated fibreboard
definition: Recycling scheme code 21 relates to mixed paper/non-corrugated fibreboard. These recyclable represent magazines, mail.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Paper
definition: Recycling scheme code 22 relates to paper. These recyclables represent letter, printer paper etc.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyvinyl Chlorides
definition: Recycling scheme code 3 relates to Polyvinyl chlorides.  These recyclables represent pipe, window profile, siding, fencing, flooring, shower curtains, lawn chairs, non-food bottles and children's toys which can be extensively recycled in Europe.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Low-density Polyethylenes
definition: Recycling scheme code 4 relates to Low-density polyethylenes.  These recyclables represent plastic bags, 6 pack rings, various containers, dispensing bottles, wash bottles, tubing, and various moulded laboratory equipment which is not often recycled through curb side programs, but some communities will accept it. Plastic shopping bags can be returned to many stores for recycling.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Steel
definition: Recycling scheme code 40 relates to steel.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Aluminium
definition: Recycling scheme code 41 relates to aluminium.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polypropylenes
definition: Recycling scheme code 5 relates to Polypropylenes.  These recyclables represent auto parts, industrial fibres, food containers, and dishware which can be recycled through some curb side programs.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Wood
definition: Recycling scheme code 50 relates to wood
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cork
definition: Recycling scheme code 51 relates to cork.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polystyrenes
definition: Recycling scheme code 6 relates to Polystyrenes.  These recyclables represent desk accessories, cafeteria trays, plastic utensils, toys, video cassettes and cases, clamshell containers, packaging peanuts, and insulation board and other expanded polystyrene products (e.g., Styrofoam) which can be recycled through some curb side programs.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cotton
definition: Recycling scheme code 60 relates to cotton.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Jute
definition: Recycling scheme code 61 relates to jute.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Plastics Other
definition: Recycling scheme code 7 relates to Other plastics, such as acrylic, nylon, polycarbonate, and polylactic acid (a bioplastic), and multilayer combinations of different plastics.  These recyclables represent Bottles, plastic lumber applications, headlight lenses, and safety shields/glasses which have traditionally not been recycled, though some curb side programs now take them.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Colourless glass
definition: Recycling scheme code 70 relates to colourless glass.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Green glass
definition: Recycling scheme code 71 relates to green glass.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Brown glass
definition: Recycling scheme code 72 relates to brown glass.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Paper and Fibreboard/Miscellaneous Metals
definition: Recycling scheme code 80 relates to composite materials paper and fibreboard/miscellaneous metals.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Paper/Fibreboard and Plastic
definition: Recycling scheme code 81 relates to composite materials paper/fibreboard and plastic.  These recyclables represent consumer packaging, pet food bags, cold store grocery bags, Ice cream containers, cardboard cans, disposable plates.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Paper and Fibreboard/Aluminium
definition: Recycling scheme code 82 relates to composite material paper and fibreboard/aluminium.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Paper and Fibreboard/Tinplate
definition: Recycling scheme code 83 relates to composite material paper and fibreboard/tinplate.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Paper and fibreboard/Plastic/Aluminium
definition: Recycling scheme code 84 relates to composite materials paper and fibreboard/plastic/aluminium. These recyclables represent liquid storage containers, juice boxes, cardboard cans, cigarette pack liners, gum wrappers, cartage shells for blanks, fireworks colouring material.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite:  Paper and Fibreboard/Plastic /Aluminium/Tinplate
definition: Recycling scheme code 84 relates to composite materials paper and fibreboard/plastic/aluminium/tinplate.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Card-stock Laminate or Biodegradable Plastic
definition: Recycling scheme code 87 relates to composite materials card-stock laminate or biodegradable plastic. These recyclables represent laminating material, special occasion cards, bookmarks, business cards, flyers/advertising.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Plastic/Aluminium
definition: Recycling scheme code 90 relates to composite materials plastic/aluminium.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Plastic/Tinplate
definition: Recycling scheme code 91 relates to composite materials plastic/tinplate.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Plastic/Miscellaneous Metals
definition: Recycling scheme code 92 relates to composition materials plastic/miscellaneous metals.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Glass/Plastic
definition: Recycling scheme code 95 relates to composite materials glass/plastic.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Glass/Aluminium
definition: Recycling scheme code 96 relates to composite materials glass/aluminium.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Glass/Tinplate
definition: Recycling scheme code 97 relates to composite materials glass/tinplate.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Composite: Glass/Miscellaneous Metals
definition: Recycling scheme code 98 relates to composite materials glass/miscellaneous metals.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Acrylonitrile butadiene
definition: Recycling scheme code ABS relates to acrylonitrile butadiene styrene.  These recyclables represent monitor/TV cases, coffee makers, cell phones, most computer plastics.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: CEN
definition: Comite Europeen de Normalisation / European Committee for Standardization) is a major provider of European Standards and technical specifications. It is the only recognized European organization according to Directive 98/34/EC for the planning, drafting and adoption of European Standards in all areas of economic activity with the exception of electrotechnology (CENELEC) and telecommunication (ETSI).
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: EKO PULLO
definition: PALPA Standas for Suomen Palautuspakkaus Oy. PALPA administers the recycling of beverage containes and promotes recycling in Finland. EKO-pullo is one of the recycling systems PALPA is administer. This is a recycling system used in Finland.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polyamide
definition: Recycling scheme code PA relates to polyamide.  These recyclables represent nylon.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: PALPA
definition: PALPA stands for Suomen Palautuspakkaus Oy. PALPA administers the recycling of beverage containers and promotes recycling in Finland. PALPA is on of the recycling systems PALPA is administer. This is a recycling system used in Finland.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Mixed glass
definition: Recycling scheme code 70 in some markets relates to mixed glass.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Other
definition: Code value not available in code list.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Renewable Carbon Content
definition: it is the renewable fraction of the total carbon content of the item, i.e. excluding all atoms and molecules which are non-carbon.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Renewable Content
definition: In the first case it is a percentage by weight of whatever item is measured.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: EN13429
definition: The CEN (the European Committee for Standardization) standard on reusable packaging
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: EN 13429  ISO 18603
definition: Both EN13429 and ISO18603
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: ISO18603
definition: ISO standards in the field of packaging and the environment Reuse
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Other
definition: Code value not available in code list.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Bar
definition: A relatively long, evenly shaped piece of some solid substance
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Coil
definition: A spiral structure made by winding a material into a series of loops. A coil may or may not have a spindle around which the loops are formed.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cone
definition:
A cone is a three-dimensional geometric
shape that tapers smoothly from a flat, round base to a point.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Cylindrical
definition: A long shape that has a circular base and an equally-sized circular top.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Polygon
definition: A plane figure that is bounded by a closed path or circuit composed of a finite sequence of equally-sized straight line segments. A polygon may have a varying number of segments or ‘faces’ resulting in different configurations, for example a 5-faced polygon: pentagon, 6-faced: hexagon, 8-faced: octagon, 12-faced: dodecahedron, etc.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Rectangular
definition: A closed planar quadrilateral with four right angles.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Spherical
definition: A perfectly round geometrical object in three-dimensional space, such as the shape of a round ball. Like a circle in two dimensions, a perfect sphere is completely symmetrical around its centre, with all points on the surface lying the same distance from the centre point.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Tablet
definition: The result of different materials being compressed into a solid block usually of small dimensions.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Unspecified
definition: Shape is not currently specified in the list. To be used as a temporary means until a specific missing value is added to the list.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Packaging cost paid by supplier.
definition: The cost of packaging is paid by the supplier
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Packaging cost paid by recipient.
definition: The cost of packaging is paid by the recipient.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Packaging cost not charged (returnable).
definition: There is no charge for packaging because it is returnable.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Safe Return Deposit.
definition: A deposit paid to guarantee the safe return of the package.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Not Reusable.
definition: The package is not reusable. The equipment may only be used once and is not reusable for the purpose for which it was designed.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Package exchangeable at the point of delivery.
definition: Package exchangeable at the point of delivery. The package may be exchanged at the point of delivery.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Repack In
definition: Repack in. Code identifying that goods should be repacked in the identified package.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Unpack From
definition: Unpack from. Code identifying that goods should be unpacked from the identified package.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Pack In.
definition: Pack in. Code identifying that goods should be packed in the identified package.
codeListDefinition: Code list developed and managed by GS1.

name: Rented
definition: The package has been/will be rented from a rental agency (e.g. CHEP pallets).
