definition: Based in the North West of England, the MK (Manchester Kosher) has dedicated teams travelling the world, certifying manufacturers of raw material, ingredients and finished retail goods to the highest standards of Kosher. The MK Kosher certification services is a division of the Manchester beis din, otherwise known as Badatz Manchester, the largest Jewish court of law in the North West of England.

name: Slovak quality label level 1
definition: The quality mark is the property of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development of the Slovak Republic. The priority of the program was to make domestic quality food products and agricultural products visible and thus their competitiveness on the domestic market. The quality mark is awarded level 1.

name: Slovak quality label level 2
definition: The quality mark is the property of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development of the Slovak Republic. The priority of the program was to make domestic quality food products and agricultural products visible and thus their competitiveness on the domestic market. The quality mark is awarded level 2.

name: SRP-Verified (Sustainable Rice Platform)
definition: The SRP-Verified (Sustainable Rice Platform) label represents the integrity of claims to sustainable best practices according to the SRP Standard, as verified through the SRP Assurance Scheme. Sustainable Rice Platform is a global alliance aiming to transform the rice sector through improving smallholder livelihoods, reducing environmental impact, and providing a sustainable supply of rice.

name: Yolo Certified Organic Agriculture
definition: YCOA (Yolo County Agricultural) Commissioner's office is one of the few counties in California to offer an organic certification program to qualified agricultural producers and handlers. The certification standards used by YCOA are the USDA's National Organic Program (NOP).  YCOA is a USDA accredited certification agency.

name: Slow cooker
definition: Cooking method used to cook food slowly over a long period of time.

name: Toast
definition: Preparation method that uses dry heat to warm and brown the surface of the product.

name: Colour palette
definition: Link to a website, file, or image containing the product's colour palette to show the full overview of the different colours of the product. The overview is mainly used by suppliers to indicate the colours with their own reference numbers and names e.g. in cosmetics for make up, nail polish, lip stick etc.

name: Accessory/Add-on included
definition: Accessory/Add-on which can be used with the Trade Item to aid/enhance in its functionality or operation.

name: Accessory/Add-on sold separately
definition: Accessory/Add-on which is sold separately, that can be used with the Trade Item to aid/enhance in its functionality or operation.

name: Warranty requirements
definition: Requirements which specify the product's warranty type (i.e., implied, express, etc.) and any terms and conditions applicable. Please refer to local regulations.

name: Bag
definition: A bag is to carry or store items. Example: In European Union a plastic bag with a wall thickness below 50 microns ( 1c of Article 3 of Directive 94/62/EC).

name: Bottle
definition: Bottles are used to contain liquid or substances such as beverages, foods, cleaning products, etc.

name: Consumption utensil
definition: An item which allows the user to extract and/or consume the content of a product.

name: Container
definition: The container is intended for preparing/storing/consuming items, such as food or non-food items.

name: Cup
definition: An item is intended for consuming products. The product is sold empty. Example: Cups for beverages.

name: Heating element
definition: A heating element is a part of an object that converts electrical energy into heat.

name: Lid
definition: A lid is designed to cover an item.

name: Mouthpiece
definition: The mouthpiece is a part of an object which comes near or in contact with one's mouth during use to inhale vapor containing nicotine, cannabis or other chemicals.

name: Reservoir
definition: The reservoir is a part of an object which contains nicotine, cannabis or other chemicals.

name: Stirrer
definition: A stirrer is used as a way to mix, blend a product.

name: Straw
definition: A straw is designed to drink a liquid by mouth.

name: Wrapper
definition: A wrapper is used for the process of enclosing all or part of an item with layer(s) of flexible wrapping material.

name: Other sustainability score
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of sustainability scores. This may be due to legal issues and/or local regulations pending (Example: Eco-score from France under litigation). Please work with a GS1 organisation to send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: End of software support
definition: Software support no longer available.

name: Loss of effectiveness
definition: Product can still be used but provided data about usability, benefit is no longer valid.

name: Loss of scent or taste
definition: The product scent or taste may no longer be as expected.

name: No customer support provided
definition: Customer support is provided with a charge or is not available.

name: No guarantee of specified results
definition: No guarantee that product still meets specified results, could have an unwanted impact or may have an undesirable effect.

name: No longer fit for consumption
definition: The product is no longer fit for consumption.

name: No longer safe to use
definition: The product is no longer safe to use.

name: Other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Possibility of increased toxicity
definition: There is a possibility the product will have an increase in toxicity.

name: Toxic
definition: Product becomes toxic.

name: Battery pack
definition: Two or more electrochemical cells electrically interconnected in an appropriate series/parallel arrangement to provide the required operating current and voltage levels.

name: Gillnets: Set (anchored) gillnets: demersal gillnets
definition: Gillnets: Set (anchored) gillnets: demersal gillnets. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for wild catch fishing gear.

name: Gillnets: Set (anchored) gillnets: pelagic gillnets
definition: Gillnets: Set (anchored) gillnets: pelagic gillnets. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for wild catch fishing gear.

name: Hand implements
definition: Hand implements (Wrenching gear, clamps, tongs, rakes, spears).

name: Seine Nets: Purse seines - with FADs
definition: Purse seines with FADs (Fish Aggregation Devices). WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for wild catch fishing gear.

name: Seine Nets: Purse seines - without FADs
definition: Purse seines without FADs (Fish Aggregation Devices). WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for wild catch fishing gear.

name: Pulse trawls
definition: Pulse trawls. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for wild catch fishing gear. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for wild catch fishing gear.

name: Bioaccumulation
definition: A hazard associated with the gradual accumulation of some chemical substances into a product's ingredients or raw materials.

name: Cardiovascular toxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with cardiovascular organs or process.

name: Dermatotoxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the skin or dermal layers.

name: Developmental toxicity
definition: Any structural or functional alteration caused by an environmental toxin causing harm or reaction that interferes with normal growth, differentiation, development, and/or behaviour.

name: Endocrine toxicity
definition: Endocrine toxicity results when a chemical interferes with the synthesis, secretion, transport, metabolism, binding action, or elimination of hormones necessary for endocrine functions resulting in loss of normal tissue function, development, growth, or reproduction.

name: Environmental persistence
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that will persist in the environment.

name: Environmental toxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances which causes environmental toxicity concerns.

name: Genotoxicity
definition: Genotoxicity is the property of chemical agents that damage the genetic information within a cell causing mutations, which may lead to cancer.

name: Hazard trait under review
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances which is under review to determine the type of toxicity which can result from the use of the product.

name: Hematotoxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the blood and blood-forming tissues.

name: Hepatotoxicity and digestive system toxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the liver or its processes.

name: Immunotoxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the immune system or on other systems as a result of immune system dysfunction.

name: Musculoskeletal toxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with muscles, tendons, and bones.

name: Nephrotoxicity and other toxicity to the urinary system
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the kidneys and their functioning.

name: Neurodevelopmental toxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with brain growth and development.

name: Neurotoxicity
definition: Adverse change in structure and/or function of the central nervous system and/or peripheral nervous system measured at the neurochemical, behavioural, neurophysiological, or anatomical levels.

name: Ocular toxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that cause one or more adverse changes that effect the structure or function of the eye.

name: Ototoxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with the ears or hearing.

name: Respiratory toxicity
definition: A hazard associated with some chemical substances that interfere in some way with respiratory system or its processes.

name: Abaca (Manila hemp)
definition: Fibre obtained from the sheathing leaf of Musa textilis.

name: Acrylic
definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules comprising at least 85% (by mass) in the chain of the acrylonitrilic pattern.

name: Alfa
definition: Fibre obtained from the leaves of Stipa tenacissima (esparto, esparto grass, halfah grass, alfa grass, or needle grass).

name: Alginate
definition: Fibre obtained from metallic salts of alginic acid.

name: Alpaca wool
definition: Alpaca hair specifically refers to the fur from the body of a alpaca, but more generally refers to the fibre (and cloth).

name: Angora wool
definition: Angora hair or Angora fibre refers to the downy coat produced by the Angora rabbit.

name: Aramid
definition: Fibre formed from synthetic linear macromolecules made up of aromatic groups joined by amide or imide linkages, of which at least 85% are joined directly to two aromatic rings and with the number of imide linkages, if present, not exceeding the number of amide linkages.

name: Bamboo
definition: Any of various woody or arborescent grasses (as of the genera Bambusa, Arundinaria, and Dendrocalamus of the subfamily Bambusoideae) of tropical and temperate regions having hollow stems, thick rhizomes, and shoots. The packaging may be in the form of paper, wood or leaves.

name: Broom fibre
definition: Fibre obtained from the base of Cytisus scoparius and/or Spartium Junceum.

name: Camel wool
definition: Camel hair specifically refers to the fur from the body of a camel, but more generally refers to the fibre (and cloth).

name: Cashmere wool
definition: Wool obtained from cashmere goats, pashmina goats and some other breeds of goat.

name: Cellulose hydrate
definition: A class of materials manufactured by the conversion of natural cellulose to a soluble cellulosic derivative and subsequent regeneration, typically forming a film (e.g., cellophane).

name: Ceramic
definition: A non-specific material made from clay and hardened by firing at a high temperatures. Examples can include terra-cotta, earthenware, stoneware, porcelain, and high-tech ceramics.

name: Chlorofibre
definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules having in their chain more than 50% by mass of chlorinated vinyl or chlorinated vinylidene monomeric units.

name: Cloth or fabric
definition: A non specific material made by weaving, felting, knitting, or crocheting natural and/or synthetic fibres.

name: Coir (coconut)
definition: Fibre obtained from the fruit of Cocos nucifera.

name: Composite
definition: A material that is made from multiple materials.

name: Natural cork
definition: Cork is an impermeable buoyant material, the phellem layer of bark tissue that is harvested for commercial use primarily from Quercus suber (the cork oak).

name: Double wall corrugated board
definition: A structure formed by two layers of corrugated cardboard (flutes), with a linerboard facing between them.

name: Corrugated board other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of corrugated boards. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Single wall corrugated board
definition: A structure formed by three layers of paper that are glued using starch into one single, sturdy sheet; also termed double faced.

name: Triple wall corrugated board
definition: A structure formed by an inner and outer liner with three fluted sheets in between, each separated by a layer of paper.

name: Cupro
definition: Regenerated cellulose fibre obtained by the cuprammonium process.

name: Elastane
definition: Elastofibre composed of at least 85% (by mass) of a segmented polyurethane, and which, when stretched to three times its original length and released, recovers rapidly and substantially to its initial length.

name: Elastodiene
definition: Elastofibre composed of natural or synthetic polyisoprene, or composed of one or more dienes polymerised with or without one or more vinyl monomers, and which, when stretched to three times its original length and released, recovers rapidly and substantially to its initial length.

name: Elastomultiester
definition: Fibre formed by interaction of two or more chemically distinct linear macromolecules in two or more distinct phases (of which none exceeds 85% by mass) which contains ester groups as the dominant functional unit (at least 85%) and which, after suitable treatment when stretched to one and half times its original length and released, recovers rapidly and substantially to its initial length.

name: Burlap fibre
definition: The American name for cloth woven from jute plant skins and other vegetable fibres. In other parts of the world it is known as Hessian, Hessian cloth, or gunny from the Indian gain.

name: Cotton
definition: A natural cellulosic seed-hair fibre, obtained from the seed pod of the cotton plant.

name: Flax
definition: The plant from the stem of which bast fibre is extracted by retting to produce linen. An erroneous term for linen fibre, particularly in blends.

name: Hemp
definition: Hemp is a commonly used term for varieties of the Cannabis plant. Hemp can yield fibre which can be used in ropes, cloths, weaves, as a reinforcement of polymer composites as well as pulps for paper making.

name: Jute
definition: A bast fibre obtained from the round pod jute or the long pod jute of the family Tiliaceae. Jute ribbon is purely made from the jute plant. Grown extensively in Pakistan and India, mainly in the Bengal district of Pakistan.

name: Fibre other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of fibre. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Fluorofibre
definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules made from fluorocarbon aliphatic monomers.

name: Solidified foam
definition: A non specific material in a lightweight cellular form resulting from introduction of gas bubbles during manufacture, used to reduce shock and vibration or abrasion.

name: Glass
definition: A substance mainly consisting of sand, lime and soda, fused at high temperatures and cooled quickly so that it solidifies to a vitreous or noncrystalline condition. This term applies to transparent clear glass or as a generic term if distinction with coloured glass is not desired.

name: Glass fibre
definition: Fibre made of glass.

name: Coloured glass
definition: Glass containing external colouring or glass that has been coloured by the addition of colouring agents/particles in its creation.

name: Goat wool
definition: Wool obtained from goats.

name: Henequen
definition: Fibre from the bast of Agave fourcroydes.

name: Horse hair
definition: Fibre made from hair of horses.

name: Kapok
definition: Fibre obtained from the inside of the kapok fruit (Ceiba pentandra).

name: Laminated carton
definition: A material made up of laminates of paperboard, foil and polyethylene which combined form a sheet suitable for asceptic processing.

name: Llama wool
definition: LIama hair specifically refers to the fur from the body of a llama, but more generally refers to the fibre (and cloth).

name: Lyocell
definition: A regenerated cellulose fibre obtained by dissolution, and an organic solvent (mixture of organic chemicals and water) spinning process, without formation of derivatives.

name: Maguey
definition: Fibre from the bast of Agave cantala.

name: Melamine
definition: Fibre formed of at least 85% by mass of cross-linked macromolecules made up of melamine derivatives.

name: Aluminium
definition: A non specific material made from aluminium or aluminium alloy.

name: Brass
definition: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.

name: Metal composite
definition:
Refers to an object that is composed of two separate metals joined together. 
Instead of being a mixture of two or more metals, like alloys, metal composites consist of layers of different metals.

name: Iron
definition: A heavy metallic element (Fe) capable of being fashioned into a variety of forms.

name: Lead
definition: A bluish-white soft malleable ductile plastic but inelastic heavy metallic element (Pb).

name: Metal other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of metal or metal alloy material. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Stainless steel
definition: An alloy of steel with chromium and sometimes another element (as nickel or molybdenum) that is practically immune to rusting and ordinary corrosion.

name: Steel
definition: Commercial iron that contains carbon in any amount up to about 1.7 percent as an essential alloying constituent, is malleable when under suitable conditions, and is distinguished from cast iron by its malleability and lower carbon content.

name: Tin
definition: Tin is a chemical element that is obtained chiefly from the mineral cassiterite, where it occurs as an oxide, SnO2. This silvery, malleable poor metal is not easily oxidized in air, and is used to coat other metals to prevent corrosion. It is used in many alloys, most notably bronze.

name: Metal fibre/Metallic fibre
definition: Manufactured fibers composed of pure metals and metallic alloys which can be processed into textile products, porous media, plastic-coated metals, etc.

name: Calcium carbonate
definition: Ground calcium carbonate and precipitated calcium carbonate products serve as functional fillers in plastic and rubber applications. Calcium carbonate is widely used as in polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyolefin, polypropylene (PP), polyethylene (PE) and unsaturated polyester resins applications.

name: Mineral other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of mineral. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Talc
definition: Talc is used to stiffen thermoplastics, mainly polypropylene but also polyethylene and polyamide (Nylon).

name: Modacrylic
definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules having in the chain more than 50% and less than 85% (by mass) of the acrylonitrilic pattern.

name: Modal
definition: A regenerated cellulose fibre obtained by a modified viscose process having a high breaking force and high wet modulus.

name: Mohair wool
definition: Mohair is wool made from the hair of the Angora goat.

name: Natural rubber
definition: A strong elastic material made by drying the sap from various tropical trees, especially the American rubber tree.

name: Other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Other animal fibre
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of fibre from animals. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Corrugated paper
definition: Heavy paper with ridges and grooves, used in packing fragile articles.

name: Kraft paper
definition: Kraft paper is the paper grade with the highest strength. It is used for the production of e.g. paper bags, emery paper or shopping bags.

name: Kraft paper (wet strength)
definition: The wet-strength kraft paper has a certain tear strength when wet due to special additives. It is used for the production of e.g. paper bags, emery paper or shopping bags.

name: Molded pulp
definition: Used for producing pulp-based or fibrous products by pressing; example products: egg packages, trays and boxes for fruits and vegetables.

name: Paper other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of paper-based material. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Paper
definition: A non-specific sheet material produced by the matting of fibres from wood, rags, or other fibrous materials. Generally, paper is of a lesser thickness or weight than paperboard.

name: Paperboard
definition: A non specific material, generally made from cotton or wood, that describe a variety or of board materials used in the production of boxes, folding cartons, and solid fibre and corrugated shipping containers; also termed cardboard.

name: Rayon paper
definition: Generic term for a manmade fibre derived from regenerated cellulose.

name: Plant leaves
definition: Plant leaves, such as banana leaves, including wet or dry leaves. In some cases, leaves are pre-softened by steaming.

name: Bioplastic
definition: Plastic materials made from biomass, but may have exactly the same properties as ordinary plastic. Sometimes these plastics are biodegradable.

name: Plastic other
definition: A non-specific material made of any of numerous organic synthetic or processed materials that are mostly thermoplastic or thermosetting polymers of high molecular weight and that can be made into objects, films, or filaments.

name: Thermoplastics
definition: A non-specific substance that becomes soft and pliable when heated, without a change in its intrinsic properties. Polystyrene and polyethylene are thermoplastics.

name: Polyethylene terephthalate, amorphous (APET)
definition: Polyethylene Terephthalate, amorphous (APET) has a very high transparency, is flame retardant and suitable for direct food contact.

name: Polypropylene, longitudinally and laterally stretched (BOPP)
definition: Biaxially oriented PP (BOPP) films are characterized by their tear, impact and puncture resistance. The film is mainly used in food packaging, e.g. as candy wrap or wrapping for chocolate bars.

name: Acetate
definition: Cellulose acetate is one of the most important esters of cellulose. Depending on the way it has been processed cellulose acetate can be used for a wide variety of applications, e.g. films, membranes or fibres.

name: Crystallized polyethylene terephthalate (CPET)
definition: Crystallized polyethylene terephthalate (CPET) is a variation of standard PET which has been crystallized for heat resistance, rigidity, and toughness.

name: Epoxy
definition: Epoxy resins are thermoset polymers which are frequently used as coatings for metal packaging such as soft-drink cans.

name: Expanded polystyrene (EPS)
definition: Expanded polystyrene is a rigid, tough, closed cell and lightweight thermoplastic foam material. It is manufactured by expanding spherical beads in a mold, using heat and pressure to fuse the beads together. While each individual bead is a closed cell environment, there are significant open spaces between each bead.

name: Ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA)
definition: Ethylene vinyl acetate, a copolymer of 60 to 90% ethylene and 40 to 10% vinyl acetate. Packaging applications include soft films, coatings, hot melt adhesives, wine cork substitutes, and closure seals for plastic and metal container caps.

name: Ethylene vinyl alcohol (EVOH)
definition: Ethylene vinyl alcohol, a copolymer of ethylene and vinyl alcohol. A plastic resin commonly used in food applications to provide barrier to oxygen and other gases.

name: High density polyethylene (HDPE)
definition: High-Density PolyEthylene (HDPE) is a polyethylene thermoplastic made from petroleum. A strong, relatively opaque form of polyethylene having a dense structure with few side branches off the main carbon backbone. Can be applied to bottles, flasks and caps.

name: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE)
definition: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is a polyethylene thermoplastic made from petroleum. A strong form of polyethylene having a less dense structure with more side branches off the main carbon backbone (on about 2% of the carbon atoms) than HDPE; therefore its tensile strength is lower, and its resilience is higherMade in translucent or opaque variations, it is quite flexible, and tough to the degree of being almost unbreakable. It is widely used for manufacturing various containers, dispensing bottles, wash bottles, tubing, plastic bags for computer components, and various moulded laboratory equipment. Its most common use is in plastic bags.

name: Linear low density polyethylene
definition: Linear low density polyethylene is a linear polyethylene with a significant number of short branches on the polymer backbone. It is commonly made by copolymerization of ethylene with longer-chain olefins. It is different from LDPE due to the absence of long chain branches which gives it higher tensile strength, impact and puncture resistance than LDPE. Common uses of LLDPE are plastic bags, wraps, stretch wraps, pouches, covers and lids.

name: Medium-density polyethylene
definition: Medium-density polyethylene is a type of polyethylene defined by a density range of 0.926-0.940 g/cm3. MDPE is typically used in shrink films, sacks, packaging film and carrier bags.

name: Nylon
definition: Packaging applications include oven-baking bags (nylon 6 and nylon 66) and barrier layers (MXD6 and nylon 6) for PET and HDPE bottles. Very occasionally, bottles can be made of nylon.

name: Oriented polypropylene (OPP)
definition: Oriented polypropylene (OPP) is made of a soft polypropylene material which is stretched in a transverse or longitudinal direction (monoaxial) and becomes therefore brittle. Also known as: biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP), CAS Registry Number: 9003-07-0

name: Polymers Other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of polymer. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Polyamide (PA)
definition: A polymer with repeating units linked by amide bonds. Polyamides (PA) occur both naturally and artificially, examples of naturally occurring polyamides are proteins, such as wool and silk. Artificially made polyamides can be nylons, aramids, and sodium poly(aspartate).

name: Polyacrylonitril (PAN)
definition: Polyacrylonitril is a organic polymer which is frequently used in fibres for textiles. As fibres the material is frequently referred to as acrylic.

name: Polycarbamide (PB)
definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules having in the chain the recurring ureylene (NH-CO-NH) functional group.

name: Polycarbonate (PC)
definition: Polycarbonate, a transparent thermoplastic which is used in a wide variety of applications including CDs and DVDs, eyeglasses, cell phone covers, laptops as well as packaging applications such as bottles.

name: Polycaprolactone (PCL)
definition: Polycaprolactone is a biodegradable polyester which is also used in in the manufacturing of polyurethanes. It is also used in blends with thermoplastic starch to improve properties and can also be used as a plasticizer to PVC.

name: Polyethylene (PE)
definition: A thermoplastic composed of the polymers of ethylene.

name: Polyethylene naphthalate (PEN)
definition: Polyethylene naphthalate is a polymer with good barrier properties (unlike Polyethylene terephthalate). It is well-suited for production of the amber-coloured bottles meant for packing beverages like beer.

name: Polyester (PES)
definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules comprising at least 85% (by mass) in the chain of an ester of a diol and terephthalic acid.

name: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET)
definition: Polyethylene terephthalate is a thermoplastic polymer resin of the polyester family and is used in synthetic fibres. Can be applied to bottles, flasks and caps.

name: Polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG)
definition: Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol (PETG) is a PET modified with glycol, which is characterized by its aqueous properties (viscosity). Applications are found in injection molding.

name: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA)
definition: Polyhydroxyalkanoates are linear polyesters produced in nature by bacterial fermentation of sugar or lipids.

name: Polyimide (PI)
definition: Fibre formed from synthetic linear macromolecules having in the chain recurring imide units.

name: Polylactic acid or Polylactide (PLA)
definition: Polylactic acid or Polylactide is a biodegradable, thermoplastic, aliphatic polyester derived from lactic acid.

name: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA)
definition: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA) is often used as a lightweight and shatterproof alternative to glass, due to its transparency, brilliance and scratch resistance, PMMA is therefore often referred to as acrylic glass.

name: Polyoxymethylene (POM)
definition: Polyoxymethylene (POM) is a thermoplastic with good mechanical properties and high dimensional stability. Fields of application are the automotive industry and electrical engineering, in packaging it is used for e.g. spray cans, gas lighter tanks, gas ampoules. Also known as acetal, polyacetal, and polyformaldehyde.

name: Polypropylene (PP)
definition: A non-specific material made of various thermoplastic plastics or fibres that are polymers of propylene.

name: Polystyrene (PS)
definition: A polymer prepared by the polymerization of styrene as the sole monomer.

name: Polyurethane (PU)
definition: Polyurethanes are primarily thermoset resins which are used in the manufacture of flexible and rigid foams, microcellular foam seals and gaskets, as well as high performance adhesives, surface coatings and sealants. Polyurethane can also be used to make synthetic fibres.

name: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)
definition: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA or PVOH) is a biodegradable and highly water soluble polymer with high gas and grease barrier. Common uses for PVA are paper adhesives, paper coatings, as a self-standing water soluble films as well as blends to improve processability of thermoplastic starch.

name: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC)
definition: A polymer of vinyl chloride used especially for electrical insulation, films, and pipes.

name: Polyvinylidene chloride (PVDC)
definition: Polyvinylidene chloride is primarily used as a barrier coating to provide barrier against fat, vapour and gases.

name: Styrene acrylonitrile (SAN)
definition: Styrene acrylonitrile (SAN) is a copolymer transparent and rigid plastic. Examples of applications are kitchenware and cosmetic packaging.

name: Thermoplastic starch (TPS)
definition: Thermoplastic starch is obtained through destructurization of natural starch through exposure to shear and heat. TPS is most frequently used in blends with biodegradable synthetic polymers such as PCL and PVA.

name: Extruded polystyrene (XPS)
definition: Extruded polystyrene is a rigid, tough, closed cell and lightweight thermoplastic foam material. It is manufactured using a process of extrusion that produces a homogeneous "closed cell" matrix with each cell fully enclosed by polystyrene walls.

name: Protein
definition: Fibre obtained from natural protein substances regenerated and stabilised through the action of chemical agents.

name: Ramie
definition: Fibre obtained from the bast of Boehmeria nivea and Boehmeria tenacissima.

name: Rubber
definition: A strong elastic synthetic substance made either by improving the qualities of natural rubber or by an industrial process using petroleum and coal products.

name: Silk
definition: Fibre obtained exclusively from silk-secreting insects.

name: Sisal
definition: Fibre obtained from the leaves of Agave sisalana.

name: Sunn hemp
definition: Fibre from the bast of Crotalaria juncea.

name: Triacetate
definition: Cellulose acetate fibre wherein at least 92% of the hydroxyl groups are acetylated.

name: Trivinyl
definition: Fibre formed of acrylonitrile terpolymer, a chlorinated vinyl monomer and a third vinyl monomer, none of which represents as much as 50% of the total mass.

name: True hemp
definition: Fibre obtained from the bast of hemp (Cannabis sativa).

name: Vinyl
definition: A non-specific polymer of a vinyl compound or a product (as a resin or a textile fibre) made from such a polymer.

name: Vinylal
definition: Fibre formed of linear macromolecules whose chain is constituted by poly(vinyl alcohol) with differing levels of acetalisation.

name: Viscose
definition: Regenerated cellulose fibre obtained by the viscose process for filament and discontinuous fibre.

name: Hardboard
definition: Hardboard (not to be confused with hardwood), also called High-Density Fiberboard (HDF), is a type of fibreboard, which is similar to particle board and medium-density fiberboard, but is denser, much stronger and harder because it is made out of exploded wood fibres which have been highly compressed. Consequently, the density of hardboard is 31 lbs or more per cubic foot (500 kg/m³)[2] and is usually about 50-65 lbs per cubic foot (800–1040 kg/m³). It differs from particle board in that the bonding of the wood fibers requires no additional materials, although resin is often added. Unlike particle board, it will not split or crack.

name: Hardwood
definition: A general term referring to any variety of broad-leaved, deciduous trees, and the wood from those trees. The term has nothing to do with the actual hardness of the wood; some hardwoods are softer than certain softwood (evergreen) species.

name: Medium density fibreboard
definition: Medium-Density Fibreboard (MDF) is an engineered wood product made by breaking down hardwood or softwood residuals into wood fibres, combining them with wax and a resin binder, and forming panels by applying high temperature and pressure. MDF is generally denser than plywood. It is made up of separated fibres, but can be used as a building material similar in application to plywood. It is stronger and much more dense than particle board.

name: Oriented strand board (OSB)
definition: Oriented Strand Board (OSB), also known as sterling board, sterling OSB, aspenite, and smartply, is an engineered wood particle board formed by adding adhesives and then compressing layers of wood strands (flakes) in specific orientations. OSB may have a rough and variegated surface with the individual strips of around 2.5 × 15 cm (1" × 6"), lying unevenly across each other and comes in a variety of types.

name: Wood other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code value and definitions of wood. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Particle board
definition: Particle Board, also known as particleboard, chipboard, and Low-Density Fibreboard (LDF), is an engineered wood product manufactured from wood chips, sawmill shavings, or sawdust, and a synthetic resin or other suitable binder, which is pressed and extruded. Particle board is a composite material.

name: Plywood
definition: Plywood, a manufactured wood panel similar to LDF, MDF, and HDF, is made from layering thin sheets of wood. Plywood layers (called veneers or plies) are glued together, with adjacent plies having their wood grain rotated relative to adjacent layers up to 90 degrees. All plywoods bind resin and wood fibre sheets (cellulose cells are long, strong and thin) to form a composite material.

name: Softwood
definition: General term used to describe lumber produced from needle and/or cone bearing trees (Conifers).

name: Wool
definition: Fibre from sheep's or lambs’ fleeces (Ovis aries) or a mixture of fibres from sheep's or lambs’ fleeces and the hair of the following animals: alpaca, llama, camel, kashmir goat, angora goat, angora rabbit, vicuna, yak, guanaco, cashgora goat, beaver, otter.

name: Boswellia resin extract
definition: GS1 Tagname Description: Resin made from Boswellia extract (bot.: Boswellia serrata) - UOM for Nutrient Panel: mg - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms: - Indian incense, Indian frankincense, CAS number: 97952-72-2

name: Gamma-Aminobutyric acid (GABA)
definition: GS1 Tagname Description: Gamma-Aminobutyric acid, or GABA, is the chief inhibitory neurotransmitter in the developmentally mature mammalian central nervous system. Its principal role is reducing neuronal excitability throughout the nervous system. GABA is known for producing a calming effect for controlling anxiety, stress and fear. - UOM for Nutrient Panel: MGM - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms: GABA, γ-Aminobutyric acid, Piperidic acid, Piperidinic acid, CAS number: 56-12-2

name: Golden poppy extract
definition: GS1 Tagname Description: Golden poppy extract (bot.: Eschscholzia californica) - UOM for Nutrient Panel: mg - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms: California poppy, California sunlight or cup of gold

name: L-Theanine
definition: GS1 Tagname Description: L-Theanine is an amino acid analogue of the proteinogenic amino acids. Theanine provides a unique brothy or savoury (umami) flavour to green tea infusions. - UOM for Nutrient Panel: MGM - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms: Theanine, CAS number: 3081-61-6

name: Manuka honey (MGO)
definition: GS1 Tagname Description: Manuka honey (MGO) is made in Australia and New Zealand by bees that pollinate the native leptospermum scoparium bush (also known as a tea tree). Advocates say it can treat wound infections and other conditions.- UOM for Nutrient Panel: MGM - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms: MGO, CAS: 91052-92-5

name: Withania somnifera
definition: GS1 Tagname Description: Withania somnifera or ashwagandha, is an evergreen shrub in the Solanaceae or nightshade family. It is most common used as a dietary supplement. - UOM for Nutrient Panel: MGM - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms: Ashwagandha, Winter Cherry, Indian Ginseng, CAS number: 90147-43-6

name: Carbon Neutral SGS (Société Générale de Surveillance)
definition: The label confirms, the audit and certification of a product’s carbon footprint by the accreditation body Société Générale de Surveillance (SGS) based on the reference of ISO standard 14067 for the carbon footprint of products (CFP).

name: Cosmos natural BDIH (Bundesverband der Industrie- und Handelsunternehmen)
definition: The Bundesverband der Industrie- und Handelsunternehmen (BDIH) COSMOS logo with signature “natural” is used to certify products which comply with the COSMOS-standard and are containing less than 20% of organic origin.

name: Cosmos organic BDIH (Bundesverband der Industrie- und Handelsunternehmen)
definition: The Bundesverband der Industrie- und Handelsunternehmen (BDIH) COSMOS logo with signature „organic“ is used to certify products which comply with the COSMOS-standard and contain the required percentages of organic ingredients (> 20%) as specified in the COSMOS standard.

name: Demeter guaranteed (garantiert)
definition: The "Biodynamisch" on the Demeter guaranteed label, indicates that products contain at least 95 percent organic and 90 percent Demeter ingredients. The label is issued by the association Demeter e.V.

name: ECOCERT natural detergent
definition: The ECOCERT logo with signature “NATURAL DETERGENT” is used to certify detergents which comply with the ECOCERT Standard. Also labeled as "Ecocert Ecodetergent"

name: ECOCERT natural detergent made with organic
definition: The ECOCERT logo with signature “NATURAL DETERGENT made with ORGANIC” is used to certify detergents which comply with the ECOCERT Standard made from at least 10% organic raw materials.

name: Flustix - completely free from plastics
definition: The label confirms that the complete product, packaging as well as content, is completely free from plastics.

name: Flustix - plastic-free packaging
definition: The label confirms that products, of any kind, are sold in a plastic-free packaging.

name: Flustix - plastic-free product
definition: This label confirms that products are plastic-free, but have to be packed in plastic due to sanitary reasons, such as medical appliances, children toys or similar.

name: Flustix - products free from microplastics
definition: The label confirms that products, especially liquid product contents, are microplastic-free. Flustix tests and certifies with its accredited partners on the basis of the only internationally respected and followed microplastic definition by European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) .

name: Flustix - products made from recycled plastics
definition: The label confirms that products are fully or partly made from recycled plastics. The percentage of recycled plastics is determined by an audit analyzing the manufacturing process and products, including packaging. The certification is awarded for goods of any kind.

name: Flustix - recyclable packaging
definition: The label confirms the recyclability of the packaging, certified by flustix.

name: Halal IIDC (Islamic Information Documentation and Certification GmbH)
definition: Halal Islamic Information Documentation and Certification GmbH (IIDC) is an independent and internationally accredited inspection and certification center for halal foods and services.

name: Halal Quality Control (HQC)
definition: Halal Quality Control (HQC) is the German certification body established in 1983, globally recognized and accredited for its Halal services.

name: Möbelfakta
definition: Möbelfakta is a sustainability label for furniture. The label is owned by IVL and Trä- och Möbelföretagen (TMF). Möbelfakta works to establish harmonized requirements for furniture that ensures sustainable development, both nationally and internationally. A piece of furniture that lives up to Möbelfakta's three parts meets the market's requirements for the environment, is manufactured in accordance with ethical guidelines and complies with international requirements specifications for quality.

name: Qualitaetszeichen Hessen (QZHE)
definition: The QZHE (Qualitaetszeichen Hessen) is a quality mark of the State of Hessen. Supervised by the Ministry for Rural Areas and Consumer Protection Hessen sourcing their natural ingredients with respect for people and biodiversity.

name: Bain-marie/Water bath
definition: A bain-marie is placing a container with food in a hot (or cold) water bath to heat (or cool) the food gently, or to keep it warm (or cold). Also known as a water bath or double boiler.

name: Aquaculture cages - (open) dam systems
definition: Aquaculture cages - (open) dam systems. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture cages - full lifecycle
definition: Aquaculture cages - full lifecycle. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture cages - wild juveniles
definition: Aquaculture cages - wild captured juveniles. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture float/tray/raft/rope/bottom-wild
definition: Aquaculture float/tray/raft/rope/bottom - wild captured juveniles. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture float/tray/raft/rope/bottom-100%
definition: Aquaculture float/tray/raft/rope/bottom - full lifecycle production. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture ponds - extensive production
definition: Aquaculture ponds - extensive production. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture ponds - intensive production
definition: Aquaculture ponds - intensive production. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture ponds - semi-intensive production
definition: Aquaculture ponds - semi-intensive Production. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture raceways
definition: Aquaculture raceways. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture recirculating systems
definition: Aquaculture recirculating aquaculture systems. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture recirculating systems - Aquaponic
definition: Aquaculture recirculating systems - aquaponic. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Aquaculture tanks
definition: Aquaculture tanks. WWF (World Wide Fund For Nature) accepted designation for aquaculture production system.

name: Base thickness
definition: Indicates the measurement of  thickness of the product's base/bottom when it is placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: The thickness of heavy-bottomed pot.

name: Usable inner bottom depth
definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable depth of the product's bottom inner rims when it is placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: The bottom inner depth of a food storage container.

name: Usable inner bottom diameter
definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable diameter of the product's inner bottom rims when it is placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: An inner bottom section of a bowl or inner bottom diameter of a flower pot.

name: Usable inner bottom width
definition: Indicates the measurement of the usable width of the product's bottom inner rims when it is placed in contact with the floor, table or other surface. Example: The bottom inner width of a food storage container.

name: Alpaca
definition: A long-haired domesticated South American mammal related to the llama, valued for its wool. Camelidae Lama L. pacos

name: Antelope
definition: A common name referring to many species of even-toed ruminant that are indigenous to various regions in Africa and Eurasia. Bovidae

name: Ape
definition: A large primate that lacks a tail, including the gorilla, chimpanzees, orangutan, and gibbons. Primates Haplorhini Simiiformes Catarrhini Hominoidea

name: Beefalo/Cattalo
definition: A hybrid animal of a cross between cattle and buffalo. Bovidae Bovinae Bovini Bovina Bos taurus, Bison bison

name: Capon
definition: A  cockerel (rooster) that has been castrated or neutered, either physically or chemically, to improve the quality of its flesh for food.

name: Cat
definition: A small domesticated carnivorous mammal with soft fur, a short snout, and retractable claws. Felidae Felinae Felis

name: Elk/Wapiti
definition: A red deer of a large race native to North America, North Asia and North Europe. Also called Wapiti. Cervidae Cervinae Cervus C. canadensis

name: Emu
definition: A flightless bird, native to Australia, that looks similar to the ostrich. Casuariidae Dromaius D. novaehollandiae

name: European robin
definition: A small thrush related to the chats, typically having a brown back with red on the breast or other colourful markings. Muscicapidae Erithacus E. rubecula

name: Finch
definition: A seed-eating songbird that typically has a stout bill and colourful plumage. Fringillidae

name: Gnu
definition: A large hoofed mammal that lives in Africa. There are two species: Black Gnu and Blue Gnu. Bovidae Alcelaphinae Connochaetes

name: Guinea pig
definition: A tailless rodent native to South American; includes the domestic guinea pig. Caviidae Cavia C. porcellus

name: Hen
definition: A female bird, especially of a domestic fowl.

name: Kangaroo
definition: A large plant-eating marsupial with a long powerful tail and strongly developed hind limbs that enable it to travel by leaping, found only in Australia and New Guinea. Macropodidae

name: Llama
definition: A domesticated South American camelid. Camelidae Lama L. glama

name: Monkey
definition: A common name referring to certain groups or species of simian mammals. Simiiformes

name: Mutton
definition: The flesh of sheep, especially mature sheep, used as food.

name: Ox
definition: An adult castrated male of any domesticated species of cattle.

name: Rhea
definition: A large flightless bird of South American grasslands, resembling a small ostrich with grayish-brown plumage. Rheidae Rhea Struthio americanus

name: Squab
definition: A culinary term for an immature domestic pigeon, typically under four weeks old.

name: Squirrel
definition: An agile tree-dwelling rodent with a bushy tail, typically feeding on nuts and seeds. Sciuridae

name: Starling
definition: A gregarious songbird with a straight bill, typically with dark lustrous or iridescent plumage but sometimes brightly coloured. Sturnidae

name: Venison
definition: The flesh of deer family or animal with antlers.

name: Water buffalo
definition: A large black domesticated buffalo with heavy swept-back horns, used as a beast of burden throughout the tropics. Bovinae Bubalus B. bubalis

name: Zebra
definition: An African wild horse with black-and-white stripes and an erect mane. Equidae Equus Hippotigris

name: Melamine sponge
definition: A sponge made from melamine foam. Also known as wonder or magic sponge/eraser.

name: Ferret
definition: Includes any animals that may be described/observed as any of the various ferrets (Mustela putorius furo) that are the domesticated form of the Mustela subgenus Putorius (polecat).

name: Hedgehog
definition: Includes any animals that may be described/observed as any of the various hedgehogs (Erinaceidae) belonging to the family of insectivores. There are 2 subfamilies: thornless rat or hair hedgehogs (Echinosoricinae) and spiny hedgehogs (Erinaceinae).

name: Pigeon
definition: A bird in the family Columbidae.

name: Use by date
definition: The "Use by" date or a derivation of use by (i.e. "Recommended use by") is defined by local requirements about the appropriate date term and the definition. These may vary by regulation and/or market conventions.

name: Animal protein
definition: Animal proteins are widely used for the formation of protein particles in the food industry, e.g., casein, whey protein, gelatin, egg proteins, and fibroin.

name: THC (Tetrahydrocannabinol)
definition: Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) is a chemical found in cannabis and is the principal psychoactive constituent.

name: 1080 x 2340
definition: The display of the product has a resolution of 1080 x 2340.

name: 2340 x 1080
definition: The display of the product has a resolution of 2340 x 1080.

name: 3088 x 1440
definition: The display of the product has a resolution of 3088 x 1440.

name: Proprietary blend
definition: GS1 Tagname Description: A proprietary blend is a term used to provide content for a specific blend or mix of ingredients. The specific nutrients in the blend are summed into one value to protect the formulation or other intellectual property. - UOM for Nutrient Panel: various as applicable - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms: Proprietary mix

name: Confit from France
definition: Confit is the generic name given to various foods immersed in a substance for both taste and preservation. This logo is a simple way of identifying French confit.

name: French toys designer
definition: This logo is a simple way of identifying French toy designers

name: Demain la Terre (Tomorrow the earth)
definition: Demain la Terre is an association under the law of 1901 of producers of fresh or processed fruits and vegetables, gathered around a common project of sustainable development.

name: French toys manufacturer
definition: This logo is a simple way of identifying French toy manufacturers

name: Fair wild
definition: Fair Wild stands for sustainability for wild plants and protection for those who collect and trade them. Our standard protects local plant species and wildlife from the effects of overexploitation, and ensures that local collectors enjoy fair working conditions.

name: Foie gras from France
definition: Foie gras is a culinary speciality made from fresh liver from the rearing and fattening by force-feeding of geese and ducks. This logo is a simple way of identifying French foie gras.

name: Smoked in France
definition: The "Fumé en France" salmon logo is gradually appearing in shops to make it easier to identify French production. It is subject to strict compliance with the French Smoked Salmon Charter.

name: Magret from France
definition: The magret is a lean meat fillet, native to the Gers cuisine, cut from the breast of a fattened goose or duck, fattened by force-feeding, the same ones used to produce confit and foie gras. This logo is a simple way of identifying French magret.

name: PME (Petite et Moyenne Entreprise) plus
definition: PME+ (Petite et Moyenne Entreprise, Small and Medium-sized Enterprise) is the label for independent French companies on a human scale, with ethical and responsible practices. The PME+ label is awarded after an annual audit carried out by Ecocert environment, according to a reference system inspired by the ISO 26000 standard.

name: Product of France
definition: This logo is a simple way of identifying French product.

name: Repairability index
definition: The reparability index is deployed on 5 categories of household appliances and electronics. This tool, provided for by the anti-waste law for a circular economy, aims to better inform consumers about the more or less repairable nature of their purchases.

name: Eco-responsible orchards
definition: The Eco-responsible orchards approach meets new consumer expectations. It marks the commitment of apple growers to production methods that respect the environment and biodiversity in the orchards, in order to offer a French apple of quality, healthy and rich in taste!

name: Committed winemakers
definition: The association Vignerons en Développement Durable (Winegrowers in Sustainable Development) brings together winegrowers who are committed to a CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) approach from the vine to the glass.

name: Zero pesticide residue
definition: The "Zero Pesticide Residue" programme guarantees consumers that products bearing the label are free of residues of active substances that are not compatible with this programme.

name: Absorbing blotter
definition: An absorbent piece of material for products, such as meat or fish, to absorb liquids such as blood or water.

name: Applicator
definition: Device to facilitate the direct application of the product.

name: Collar
definition: Decorative element generally imprinted and placed on the neck of bottles.

name: Threaded spindle
definition: Device with a screw system that contains a lead the consumer can lower or raise the platform. Example: Deodorant with a twist mechanism to use the product.

name: Window
definition: Transparent element affixed to a packaging to allow the consumer to see the product through it.

name: Borosilicate glass
definition: Glass composed of silicon, boron, sodium and aluminum oxides (+ other alkaline oxides). It is a technical glass, not recyclable.

name: Crystal glass
definition: Glass rich in lead oxide. It is a technical glass, not recyclable, typically used in decorative objects and also in certain cosmetic packaging.

name: Metal zamac
definition: Zamac is a family of alloys with a base metal of zinc and alloying elements of aluminium, magnesium, and copper.

name: Polymer ionomer
definition: Ionically is a cross-linked polyethylene (ionomer), can be used in combination with PE for its barrier properties.

name: Polymer mix
definition: A polymer blend or mixture of least two polymers that are blended to create a new material with different physical properties. These tend to be a proprietary mix of polymers and cannot be separated. The individual materials may not be known by the seller.

name: Polymer silicone
definition: Polymer is generally composed of organic chains linked together by the silicon-oxygen bond. Used in particular for valves. Also know as polysiloxane.

name: Expanded Polyethylene
definition: EPE is foamed polyethylene, which is a type of environmentally friendly material, that is, pearl cotton like. EPE is made of low-density polyethylene grease through a physical foaming process to produce a non-crosslinked closed cell structure. EPE can be recycled and allows a certain amount of EPE recycled material to be matched in the manufacturing process. Also known as EPE Foam.

name: Berlingot
definition: Packaging most often tetrahedral or cylindrical in shape used to contain liquids.

name: Capsule
definition: Small packaging element generally cylindrical with round edges and containing any substances like liquids, small objects like toys, coffee capsules.

name: Hanger
definition: A support for hanging products. Can be curved, triangular, or other various shapes.

name: Syringe
definition: Device consisting of a piston and a cylindrical pump body, which is used for administering, for example a liquid or joint compound.

name: Hunted/Gathered
definition: The place where wild animals may be hunted/trapped/caught or where wild vegetation may be gathered/harvested/picked.

name: Product image formed
definition: An image of a product that has the supporting shape/form (for example a model, mannequin, hanger) removed to give the product a 3-D look.

name: Not sterilised
definition: The product is not sterilised by the manufacturer.

name: Elastolefin
definition: Fibre composed of at least 95% (by mass) of macromolecules partially cross-linked, made up from ethylene and at least one other olefin and which, when stretched to one and a half times its original length and released, recovers rapidly and substantially to its initial length.

name: Quartz
definition: A hard white or colourless mineral consisting of silicon dioxide, found widely in igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks.

name: Veterinary Notification Number (NN) - Canada
definition: This is the notification number for veterinary health product that has been approved for sale in Canada.

name: Aloe vera
definition: A gelatinous substance obtained from a kind of aloe. E.g., used in cosmetics, food.

name: Coenzyme Q10 Ubiquinone
definition: A coenzyme family that is ubiquitous in animals and most bacteria.

name: Natural colour
definition: Indicates a colour additive that has been derived from a natural source to be added to a product for the primary reason of modifying the colour of the product.

name: Shea butter
definition: A fatty substance obtained from the nuts of the shea tree. E.g., used in cosmetics, food.

name: Vitamin D3
definition: A sterol C27H43OH that is a natural form of vitamin D found especially in fish, egg yolks, and fish-liver oils and is formed in the skin on exposure to sunlight or ultraviolet rays.

name: Algae oil
definition: GS1 Tagname Description: Algae oil is a food supplement with omega-3 fatty acids. - UOM for Nutrient Panel: - GS1 Notes, Keywords, and Examples: - GS1 Comment: GS1 temporary code - GS1 Synonyms:

name: Aktivstall fuer Schweine
definition: Aktivstall fuer Schweine guarantees that every farm with active housing is QS (Quality Seal) and ITW (Animal Welfare Initiative) certified.

name: Almo Tierwohl
definition: The Almo label stands for the oxen's life in the wild, on local mountain pastures and meadows. They are fed with herbs, grass and fresh water. During winter months, they are kept in spacious free-range stables where they are fed only GMO-free feed.

name: Bauern Liebe
definition: Bauern Liebe guarantees more animal welfare, sustainability and appreciation of farmers. This means more animal welfare in livestock farming and sustainability in agriculture combined with fair conditions and special bonus payments for the farmers.

name: DLG 2 Sterne Bronze (Deutsche Landwirtschafts-Gesellschaft)
definition: The DLG (Deutsche Landwirtschafts-Gesellschaft, German Agricultural Society) 2 star bronze label guarantees the second level of the DLG programme's standard in terms of animal husbandry on the participating dairy farms.

name: DLG 3 Sterne Silver (Deutsche Landwirtschafts-Gesellschaft)
definition: The DLG (Deutsche Landwirtschafts-Gesellschaft, German Agricultural Society) 3 star silver label guarantees the third level of the DLG programme's standard in terms of animal husbandry on the participating dairy farms.

name: DLG 4 Sterne Gold (Deutsche Landwirtschafts-Gesellschaft)
definition: The DLG (Deutsche Landwirtschafts-Gesellschaft, German Agricultural Society) 4 star gold label guarantees the highest standard of the DLG programme's standard in terms of animal husbandry on the participating dairy farms.

name: Fair Mast
definition: Fair Mast guarantees a modern and a more animal-friendly poultry farming, compliance with standards in the rearing of the animals and fulfil the criteria of the German Animal Welfare Association's label "Für Mehr Tierschutz".

name: Initiative Tierwohl
definition: The Animal Welfare Initiative provides more orientation for the consumer. It guarantees that meat products come from a farm that participates in the Animal Welfare Initiative.

name: Lonki Gutes Leben
definition: Lonki guarantees more animal-friendly and sustainable meat production in the field of rabbit products. The requirements aim to improve animal welfare with measurable and verifiable criteria.

name: Lonki Park
definition: Lonki Parks guarantees a group keeping of rabbits in parks.

name: Nature and Respect
definition: The Nature & Respect label guarantees core values of sustainable poultry farming, where breeders committed to provide high quality poultry.

name: Olivia Pannon White
definition: The Olivia Pannon guarantees the conformity of rabbit meat production with the requirements of the husbandry system.

name: Olivia Pannon White Plus
definition: The Olivia Pannon White+ guarantees that the production of rabbit meat complies with the requirements of the husbandry system.

name: Pro Weideland
definition: The Pro Weideland label guarantees that raw materials have been sourced with special consideration for animal welfare. Only partners who opt for the more complex but more sustainable grassland farming method and meet specific criteria are allowed to use it.

name: QM Milch (Qualitätsmanagement Milch)
definition: QM (Qualitätsmanagement Milch) guarantees quality standards for milk production for dairy farms. The QM standard ensures quality of the product as well as a transparent and traceable production process.

name: QM Milch+ (Qualitätsmanagement Milch)
definition: The QM+ (Qualitätsmanagement Milch) add-on module ensures an even more animal-friendly and sustainable milk production than QM. The QM+ add-on has been developed to promote animal welfare on dairy farms.

name: Qualivo
definition: Qualivo guarantees high quality meat and high control standards.

name: Relax Rabbit
definition: The RelaxRabbit guarantees a careful and constant monitoring of the production of rabbit meat. The production is based on IFS (International Featured Standards).

name: Tierschutzbund 1 Stern
definition: The Tierschutzbund 1 star label guarantees improvements and standards for animals. The entry level (1 gold star) offers a first clear added value for the animals with more space, structures and activity opportunities.

name: Par fry/Pre fry
definition:
Cooking method where food is partially fried. Final cooking or preparation will be accomplished by the end user of the product (e.g., french fries).
Other common names for this preparation type: parfry, par-fry, par fry and pre-fry.

name: Pharmaceutical Drugs/Medical Devices
definition: The Pharmaceutical Drugs/Medical Devices images refers to products (medical devices or pharmaceutical drugs and components) used in the diagnosis, treatment or prevention of disease that achieves its primary intended purpose through pharmacological, immunological or metabolic means within or on the body. Includes medical equipment and supplies, all drugs, biologicals or therapeutic nutritionals for human applications.

name: Regulated product content website
definition: Link for a regulatory or industry governed product content website containing product specific information.

name: Size Comparison
definition: An image that makes clear the actual size of the product, e.g., via a schematic depiction of a person or well-known object (e.g., one-euro coin) in the background.

name: Discrete content
definition: Cannabinoid content is measured relative to individual units of the product. Example: Cannabinoid content in a cannabis gummy.

name: Content
definition: The cannabinoid content stated as the total amount found in the product package. Example: Cannabinoid content in a bag of cannabis gummies.

name: Cannabidiolic acid (CBDA)
definition: Cannabidiolic acid (CBDA) is found in the cannabis plant and it is the chemical precursor to cannabidiol (CBD). Also known as: CRM, β-Resorcylic Acid. CAS number: 1244-58-2

name: Delta-8 THC (D8-THC)
definition: Delta-8-tetrahydrocannabinol (Delta-8 THC) is a psychoactive cannabinoid found in the cannabis plant. CAS number: 5957-75-5

name: Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)/Delta-9 THC
definition: Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or Delta-9 THC is the principal psychoactive constituent of cannabis. CAS number:  1972-08-3

name: Tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA)
definition: Tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA) is a precursor of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), an active component of cannabis. CAS number: 23978-85-0

name: Tetrahydrocannabivarin (THCV)
definition: Tetrahydrocannabivarin (THCV) is a homologue of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) which produce psychoactive effects. CAS number: 31262-37-0

name: Cannabidiol (CBD)
definition: Cannabidiol (CBD) is a compound that is one of the main constituents of cannabis, having mild psychoactive effects. CAS number: 13956-29-1

name: Cannabichromene (CBC)
definition: Cannabichromene (CBC) is found in the cannabis plant. It is an anti-inflammatory which may contribute to the pain-killing effect of cannabis. It is also called cannabichrome, cannanbichromene, pentylcannabichromene or cannabinochromene. CAS number: 20675-51-8

name: Cannabigerol (CBG)
definition: Cannabigerol (CBG) is a compound found in the cannabis plant.  CBG is the decarboxylated form of cannabigerolic acid, the parent molecule from which other cannabinoids are synthesised. CAS number:  25654-31-3

name: Cannabinol (CBN)
definition: Cannabinol (CBN) is a mildly psychoactive cannabinoid found in trace amounts from cannabis. CAS number: 521-35-7

name: THC-0 acetate (THC-0)
definition: THC-0-acetate (THC-0) is the acetate ester of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). CAS number: 23132-17-4

name: Delta-10 THC (D10-THC)
definition: Delta-10 -tetrahydrocannabinol (Delta-10 THC) is a psychoactive cannabinoid found in trace amounts in the cannabis plant. CAS number: 95588-87-7

name: Indica Dominant
definition: A species of Cannabis native to India and neighbouring countries. Indica strains often have higher levels of Cannabidiol (CBD), but the tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) content isn’t necessarily less. - Family/Genus/Species: Cannabaceae/Cannabis/C. indica

name: Sativa Dominant
definition: A species of Cannabis native to Eastern Asia. Sativa often has lower doses of Cannabidiol (CBD) and higher doses of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC).- Family/Genus/Species: Cannabaceae/Cannabis/C. sativa

name: Ruderalis
definition: A species of Cannabis native to Central and Eastern Europe, and Russia. It contains a relatively low quantity of psychoactive compound tetrahydrocannabinol (THC).- Family/Genus/Species: Cannabaceae/Cannabis/C. ruderalis

name: Medium-Chain triglycerides (MCT) oil
definition: Medium chain triglycerides (MCTs) are fats commercially extracted from coconut oil and palm kernel oil.

name: Sunflower oil
definition: Sunflower oil is the non-volatile oil pressed from the seeds of sunflower.

name: Butane
definition: Butane is a highly volatile, colourless hydrocarbon gas with an odour similar to petroleum. Also known as n-butane. CAS number: 106-97-8

name: Heat
definition: Heat is a form of energy crossing the boundary of a thermodynamic system by virtue of a temperature difference across the boundary.

name: Isopropanol
definition: Isopropanol is a clear, colourless liquid flammable organic compound with a pungent alcoholic odour. Also known as isopropyl alcohol. CAS number: 67-63-0

name: Dry sieve
definition: Dry Sieve is a concentrate free of chemicals and water, created by dry sifting material through a series of screens.

name: Water
definition: Water is a substance with the chemical formula H2O. Water is an inorganic, transparent, tasteless, odourless, and nearly colourless substance. CAS number: 7732-18-5

name: Hexane
definition: Hexane is an organic compound, a colourless liquid and odourless when pure. It is widely used as solvent. CAS number: 110-54-3

name: Alcohol
definition: Alcohol is an organic compound in which a hydroxyl group is bound to a carbon atom. CAS number: 64-17-5

name: Carbon dioxide
definition: Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CO2. It appears as a colourless odourless gas at atmospheric temperature and pressure. CAS number: 124-38-9

name: Ethanol
definition: Ethanol is an organic compound, a volatile, flammable, colourless liquid with a characteristic wine-like odour and pungent taste. It is the active ingredient in alcoholic drinks. Also known as ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol, drinking alcohol. CAS number: 64-17-5

name: Auto flowering
definition: The plants flower after certain amount of time, regardless of light reduction.

name: Photo period
definition: The plants flower based on the length of light and dark periods.

name: Dry machine
definition: Trimming flower, buds, or leaves using trimming machine after the plant is dried.

name: Wet machine
definition: Trimming flower, buds, or leaves using trimming machine before plant is dried.

name: Other
definition: Any other trimming process.

name: Wet hand
definition: Trimming flower, buds, or leaves by hand before plant is dried.

name: Dry hand
definition: Trimming flower, buds, or leaves by hand after the plant is dried.

name: HID (High intensity discharge)
definition: High Intensity Discharge (HID) is an overarching term for a gas-discharge light. HID lamps produce light by sending an electrical charge or “arc” between two tungsten electrical conductors (electrodes) and through an ionized gas (also known as “plasma”) which is housed inside the bulb.

name: High pressure sodium
definition: High pressure sodium light is a specific type of gas- discharge light (also known as a high intensity discharge, HID or arc light). The arc tube is made of aluminum oxide and the sodium metal is combined with several other elements like mercury which counter-balances the yellow glow with some white to light emissions.

name: Plasma induction
definition: Plasma induction is a type of high temperature plasma generated by electromagnetic induction, usually coupled with argon gas.

name: Metal halide
definition: Metal halide light device produces light by an electric arc through a gaseous mixture of vaporized mercury and metal halides.

name: LED (Light Emitting Diode)
definition: Light-emitting diode (LED) is a semiconductor device that emits light when current flows through it. Electrons in the semiconductor recombine with electron holes, releasing energy in the form of photons.

name: Sun assisted
definition: Sun light used to assist in a particular time of the day or season to mimic ideal summer growing conditions. Used along with the LED or HID light.

name: Sunlight
definition: Sunlight is solar radiation that is visible at Earth's surface.

name: Renewable material, Mass balance
definition: Renewable material and renewable feedstock (raw material used in industrial process or as fuel) with virgin raw materials in the production process. This creates a final product that is a mixture of virgin and renewable content. Mass balance is about mixing fossil and renewable/recycled materials.  It's important to note that individual packaging may not necessarily include renewable material, but the plastic material producer is certified for mass balance and incorporates a specific percentage of renewable materials in their feedstock. Refer to local regulations.

name: Recycled material, Mass balance
definition: Recycled material and feedstock are combined with virgin raw materials in the production process, resulting in a final product that contains both virgin and recycled content. Mass balance involves mixing fossil and recycled/renewable materials to meet this objective. It's important to note that individual packaging may not necessarily include recycled material, but the plastic material producer is certified for mass balance and incorporates a specific percentage of recycled materials in their feedstock. Refer to local regulations.

name: Made with/from
definition: A claim that the packaging is manufactured with/from a specific feature, and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer. Please refer to any local regulations that determine containment levels for the claim.

name: Made with/from 100%
definition: A claim that the packaging is 100% manufactured with/from a specific feature, and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer. Please refer to any local regulations that determine containment levels for the claim.

name: Partially made with/from
definition: A claim that the packaging is partially manufactured with/from a specific feature, and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the consumer. Please refer to any local regulations that determine containment levels for the claim.

name: Biodegradable material
definition: Biodegradable refers to the ability of things to get disintegrated (decomposed) by the action of micro-organisms such as bacteria or fungi biological (with or without oxygen) while getting assimilated into the natural environment.

name: Wind power
definition: Wind power or wind energy is mostly the use of wind turbines to generate electricity. Wind power is a popular, sustainable, renewable energy source that has a much smaller impact on the environment than burning fossil fuels.

name: Biogas
definition: Biogas is a naturally occurring and renewable source of energy, resulting from the breakdown of organic matter.

name: Recycled material
definition: A recycled material refers to any substance that has undergone a process of reprocessing or reclamation to be used again in the manufacturing of new products. Recycled materials can encompass a wide range of items, including paper, glass, metal, plastics, textiles, and more.

name: Renewable material
definition: A renewable material is a material made of natural resources that can be replenished.

name: Non-water soluble
definition: An adhesive that is made with components that are all not water soluble (i.e., will not dissolve in water).

name: Alkaline soluble
definition: An adhesive which is alkaline soluble or releasable.

name: Water soluble
definition: An adhesive which is water soluble or water releasable.
