name: Climate activator
definition: The Climate Activator Certified standard gives you the acknowledgement that the results of your work are helping and are meaningful. The steps that have been taken are expertly tested against published criteria in a transparent process. With the logo, you can clearly communicate your commitment to your stakeholders, who are becoming more critical when it comes to socially, ecologically and economically responsible business.

name: Contrôle Officiel Suisse des Chronomètres
definition: COSC-certified watches must be accurate to within -4 to +6 seconds per day when tested for accuracy over 15 days.

name: EKO 1
definition: EKO stars stands for organic products of Dutch origin that meet extra requirements in the field of nature, biodiversity, animal and climate as determined per sector. All these extras realised by EKO farmers in the Netherlands are indicated with the EKO 3-star quality mark, where 1 star stands for 30-60% Dutch origin.
externalLink: EKO keurmerk - Voor pioniers in biologische voeding. (eko-keurmerk.nl)

name: EKO 2
definition: EKO stars stands for organic products of Dutch origin that meet extra requirements in the field of nature, biodiversity, animal and climate as determined per sector. All these extras realised by EKO farmers in the Netherlands are indicated with the EKO 3-star quality mark, where 2 stars stand for 60-90% Dutch origin.
externalLink: EKO keurmerk - Voor pioniers in biologische voeding. (eko-keurmerk.nl)

name: EKO 3
definition: EKO stars stands for organic products of Dutch origin that meet extra requirements in the field of nature, biodiversity, animal and climate as determined per sector. All these extras realised by EKO farmers in the Netherlands are indicated with the EKO 3-star quality mark, where 3 stars stand for 90-100% Dutch origin.
externalLink: EKO keurmerk - Voor pioniers in biologische voeding. (eko-keurmerk.nl)

name: Geneva seal
definition: Geneva Seal, also known as the Poinçon de Genève, indicates a watch movement was assembled, adjusted, and cased in Geneva. The Geneva Seal also includes testing for a watch's functionality, accuracy, power reserve, and water resistance.

name: IP Suisse - Mehl Farine
definition: IP Suisse - Ingredient flour which is produced environmentally friendly.

name: MOSA certified organic
definition: Midwest Organic Services Association (MOSA) Certified Organic is an organic certifier in the United States, primarily certifying livestock and dairy.

name: NRW certified quality (NRW geprüfte Qualität)
definition: The "NRW geprüfte Qualität" label guarantees the quality of food products and their origin in North Rhine-Westphalia.

name: OK condoms
definition: Seal of approval for condoms. The association Gütesiegel für Präservative, Lucerne, certifies condoms that meet their requirements. Such condoms may use the label, on packaging, promotional material and digitals.

name: Origin mark Germany (Herkunftskennzeichnung Deutschland)
definition: The "Herkunftskennzeichen Deutschland" label guarantees that food and agricultural products are produced and manufactured in Germany.

name: QM Milch++ (Qualitätsmanagement Milch)
definition: The QM++ (Quality Management Milk) add-on module enables even more animal-friendly milk production than QM and QM+. The QM++ add-on module has been developed to further promote animal welfare on dairy farms. Cows are raised in outdoor climate conditions and can move freely.

name: QM Milch+++ (Qualitätsmanagement Milch)
definition: The QM+++ (Quality Management Milk) add-on module enables even more animal-friendly milk production than QM, QM+ and QM++. The QM+++ add-on module has been developed to further promote animal welfare on dairy farms. Cows are raised in pasture conditions and have additional outdoor access all year round.

name: Qualité Fleurier
definition: The QUALITE FLEURIER quality label is delivered by the Fleurier Quality Foundation (FQF), also known as Foundation Qualité Fleurier, to finished mechanical watches developed in Switzerland.

name: Sustainable winegrowing Portugal
definition: ViniPortugal has created the National Sustainability Certification Benchmark for the wine sector (RNCSSV), a unified reference for sustainability in wine production throughout the country, based on OIV-VITI Resolution 641-2020 'Guide to the Implementation of the Principles of Sustainable Winegrowing'.

name: Swiss made
definition: The "Swiss Made" label is a reference in the field of watchmaking, and ensures the presence of Swiss know-how in the making of the timepiece. This label reflects a quality requirement from a technical and aesthetic point of view. At present, it is a federal ordinance that sets the conditions for a timepiece to bear the Swiss Made label. While there is not a specific logo or seal, the requirements set forth the placement and styling of the words "Swiss Made" (or language equivalents) on the face of the timepiece.

name: Vipère
definition: The Viper seal is a quality certificate for mechanical chronometers delivered by the Besançon observatory.

name: Where Food Comes From organic
definition: Certificate from Where Food Comes From, Inc., related to organic products.

name: Cage
definition: A cage container or cage pallet is a type of storage or transportation unit designed with a rigid framework of bars or mesh, resembling a cage. It is typically used to securely hold, protect, and transport goods, materials while allowing for ventilation, visibility, and containment.

name: Milk mixture
definition: A mixture of raw milk and pasteurised or thermised milk, or a mixture of microfiltered skimmed milk and whole raw milk or raw cream.

name: Thermisation
definition: Thermisation is a heat treatment process applied at lower temperature than pasteurisation. The product is heated to a temperature of more than 40°C and less than 72°C for at least 15 seconds, e.g., for milk.

name: Barrel diameter
definition: Measurement of the internal width of a barrel.

name: Bend angle
definition: Angle formed between a bent structures parts, typically used to describe the deflection of material.

name: Inner diameter
definition: The measurement of the internal diameter, e.g., of a tube or pipe, measured from one inner wall to the opposite inner wall, passing through the centre.

name: Outer diameter
definition: The measurement of the total diameter, e.g., of a tube or pipe, measured from one outer wall to the opposite outer wall, passing through the centre.

name: Gauge
definition: A measurement of the thickness, size, or capacity of an object or material.

name: Grit size
definition: The size of the abrasive particles in a material, often used in sanding and polishing.

name: Handle diameter
definition: The measurement of the width across the circular cross-section of a handle.

name: Handle width
definition: Measurement of the side-to-side dimension of a handle.

name: Leg height
definition: Vertical measurement from the bottom to the top of a leg, often referring to furniture or anatomy.

name: Maximum travel distance
definition: The furthest distance a mechanism or vehicle can move within its designed limits.

name: Ramp width
definition: The horizontal measurement from one side of a ramp to the other, affecting accessibility and use.

name: Tabletop thickness
definition: Measurement of the vertical dimension of a table's surface.

name: Aging
definition: A product that is designed specifically for older/senior life stage.

name: Damaged
definition: Damaged or stressed skin is out of balance and consequently shows as a result redness and discomfort such as burning, tightness or itching.

name: Hypersensitive
definition: The term hypersensitivity is used in medicine to describe a general hypersensitivity of the skin to certain microorganisms, substances or stimuli. Hypersensitivity is a generic term for allergy, pseudo-allergy, intolerance and idiosyncrasy.

name: Medium
definition: Medium is a term widely used to refer to skin which is characterized between Normal and Dry.

name: Fabric
definition: A material made by weaving, knitting, or bonding fibers together, used primarily in textiles.

name: Brushing (external)
definition: The product can be cleaned by moving a brush across its external surface.

name: Brushing (internal)
definition: The product can be cleaned by using a pipe carrier to brush the cavity or lumen of a hollow surgical instrument. Consult the Instructions for Use (IFU) or cleaning, disinfection and sterilisation regulations for the specifications.

name: Flushing
definition: The product can be cleaned by passing liquid through the cavity or lumen of a hollow surgical instrument. Consult the Instructions for Use (IFU) or cleaning, disinfection and sterilisation instructions for the specifications of the liquid and method.

name: Soaking
definition: The product can be cleaned by leaving it in liquid for a certain amount of time to clean or soften contamination.

name: Ultrasonication
definition: The product can be cleaned using sound waves sent through a cleaning fluid. Consult the Instructions for Use (IFU) or cleaning, disinfection and sterilisation regulations for the specifications of the frequency of the sound waves.

name: Water rinsing
definition: The product can be cleaned simply with water, without the use of soap, detergent or other cleaning agents.

name: Intensive tint (level 3)
definition: Lasts about 6 to 8 weeks. Penetrates deeper into the hair and contains weak developers (hydrogen peroxide) that store the colour pigments in the hair, but cannot completely lighten the hair. E.g., semi-permanent colourations or glossings.

name: Other
definition: The value needed is not listed or is not defined within this list’s individual code values and definitions. Please send a work request into GS1 or your solution provider requesting the code you are searching for.

name: Temporary colouration (level 1)
definition: Lasts until the next hair wash. This type of colour only lays on the outer layer of the hair (cuticle) and does not penetrate the inside of the hair. E.g., colour sprays, chalk or foam colourations.

name: Washable colouration / tinting (level 2)
definition: About 6 to 10 washes. Penetrates easily into the cuticle, but not deep into the hair. Gradually fades without leaving visible roots. E.g., easily washable tints or foam tints.

name: SR416
definition: Silver oxide button cells identified by IEC name SR416 and other common names : SR416SW, 337

name: Sahti
definition: Sahti is a traditional Finnish unfiltered beer brewed with fresh yeast. The raw materials used are mainly barley malt and, in small quantities, rye malt, and sometimes wheat and oats.

name: Brand label
definition: A product that is not produced strictly for a trading partner or a purchasing group. It can be sold through any retailers. The formula/design is owned by the manufacturer, not the ultimate recipient trading partner or purchasing group. Also known as national brand.

name: Cadmium
definition: A soft, silver-white or blue, lustrous metal typically found in mineral deposits with lead, zinc, and copper.

name: Colour
definition: Colour is defined as colour found without any specific chemical synthesis, but not specified as natural colour.

name: Flavour
definition: Flavours are defined as flavours found without any specific chemical synthesis, but not specified as natural flavours.

name: Organotin
definition: Organotin substances (organotins) are tin compounds having 1, 2, 3 or 4 organic groups attached and are designated as mono-, di-, tri- or tetra-organotin depending on the number of tin-carbon bonds in the molecule. E.g., tributyltin, dibutyltin.

name: Volatile organic compound (VOC)
definition: An organic compound that has a high vapor pressure at room temperature and low water solubility.

name: Zeolite
definition: Zeolite is a group of porous minerals composed of aluminum silicates. Zeolites are used in industry for applications such as filtration, odour removal, molecular sieves, and water softening.

name: No
definition: A claim that a product does not contain (verifiably) the substance in the ClaimElementCode. Note the amount that determines containment or lack of containment is based on target market regulations.

name: European-Brewing-Convention (EBC) colour scale
definition: The EBC colour scale is a system used to measure and describe the colour of beer and wort. It is standardized by the European Brewery Convention and is widely used in Europe and internationally. The EBC value represents the depth of colour, with lower values indicating paler beers (like lagers) and higher values indicating darker beers (like stouts or porters).

name: AMOLED
definition: Active Matrix Organic Light Emitting Diode (AMOLED) is an advanced display technology where each pixel emits its own light without the need for backlighting.

name: Front projection
definition: Display method where an image is projected onto a screen from the front, typically using a projector placed in front of the viewing surface. It is commonly used in home theaters, classrooms, and cinemas.

name: Quantum dot
definition: Quantum dot is a display technology that uses quantum dots to enhance colour and brightness. Unlike OLED, quantum dot screens still require a backlight (usually LED), but they offer high brightness, vibrant colours, and long lifespan. Also known as Quantum Dot Light Emitting Diode (QLED), Triluminos, Quantum Color, or Quantum Nano-Emitting Diode (QNED).

name: Antibacterial
definition: The product is designed to contribute to hygiene or odour reduction by inhibiting the growth of bacteria on its surface or on the applied surface.

name: Permanent colouration (level 4)
definition: Permanent dyeing that does not wash out. Penetrates deep into the hair structure and changes the natural pigments through chemical reactions. This often uses ammonia or a similar alkalizing agent that opens the cuticle and hydrogen peroxide to lighten or prepare the hair. Does not wash out, needs to grow out or be refreshed by re-dyeing. E.g., classic hair dyes for a permanent change.

name: Fresh air barn
definition: A husbandry system where animals have access to different climate zones.

name: Indoor with more place
definition: A husbandry system where animals are housed in a barn (indoor) with more space per animal than the minimum legal requirements. The determination of this is made by the supplier and may be subject to target market regulations or trade organization guidelines.

name: Non labelled portion
definition: A specific husbandry system is not indicated for the ingredients of animal origin contained in the product.

name: Formed
definition: The image is of the product which has the supporting shape/form (for example a model, mannequin, hanger) removed to give the product a 3-D look.

name: Device / not multi component
definition: The code applicable for standard devices that are neither systems nor procedure packs (in accordance with the Art. 22 MDR), nor kits (only applicable in case of IVDR Art. 2).

name: Chlorhexidine gluconate
definition: A gluconate salt form of chlorhexidine, a biguanide compound used as an antiseptic agent.

name: EcoStep-Wein
definition: EcoStep-Wein is an integrated management system for small and medium-sized wineries and sparkling wine producers. It combines requirements from international standards like ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 22000, and ISO 45001. Developed with Geisenheim University and the Environmental Alliance of Hesse, it aims to optimize operations and enhance sustainability in economic, ecological, and social aspects.

name: Responsible fisheries management
definition: Responsible Fisheries Management (RFM) Certification is a voluntary and internationally accredited third-party certification program for wild-capture fisheries. It allows companies to demonstrate responsible sourcing to their customers. Certified Sustainable RFM fisheries are independently assessed and scored against strict and comprehensive criteria to ensure biological sustainability, conservation, biodiversity, and ecosystem integrity.

name: Vignerons indépendants de France
definition: The Vignerons Indépendants de France (Independent Winemakers of France) is an association of winemakers who grow their own vines, produce their own wine, and sell it directly to consumers. Their logo, a winemaker carrying a barrel, helps consumers identify authentic independent producers.

name: End of an agreed delivery period
definition: The date of the end of an agreed delivery period in which the deliveries are made.

name: Dyeing
definition: The place where the product is coloured using dyes.

name: Finishing
definition: The place where the product undergoes final treatments to enhance its quality, appearance, or performance.

name: Garment making
definition: The place where the product is cut, assembled, and sewn into its final form.

name: Mounting
definition: The place where components, embellishments, or accessories are attached to the product during production.

name: Printing
definition: The place where patterns, graphics, or text are applied to the product.

name: Stitching
definition: The place where parts of the product are joined using stitching or sewing techniques.

name: Weaving/Knitting
definition: The place where the product is formed through weaving or knitting processes.

name: Competition Act
definition: Competition act encompasses several pivotal environmental-related additions designed to hold companies accountable for their environmental claims. These provisions aim to mitigate the pervasive issue of greenwashing, ensuring businesses can't make superficial or misleading claims about their environmental efforts. For example the Canadian Competition Act.

name: No sterilisation required
definition: Sterilisation by a healthcare provider prior to use of the healthcare product is not required.

name: UDI Registry
definition: Trade channel where medical devices are applicable for a UDI database, e.g., EUDAMED, swissdamed.

name: Assorted
definition: The product is composed of an assortment of flavours/scents.

name: Plain
definition: The product is unflavoured. No flavour/scent is added. Also known as natural or nature.

name: Red fruit
definition: The product has ingredient(s) that causes the flavour/scent of red fruit.

name: Yellow fruit
definition: The product has ingredient(s) that causes the flavour/scent of yellow fruit.

name: BK04
definition: BK04 – Product classification for the Swedish building materials trade, also forming the basis for the building material index.

name: Pharmacy Product Number
definition: The Pharmacy Product Number (PPN) is a globally unique identifier for pharmaceutical products, used to ensure traceability within the supply chain. It is typically encoded in a 2D data matrix on packaging and issued under the authority of the IFA (Informationsstelle für Arzneispezialitäten) as the official issuing agency.

name: SUKL code (Slovakia)
definition: The ŠÚKL code is a unique identifier used by the State Institute for Drug Control (ŠÚKL) in Slovakia. It uniquely identifies a specific medicinal product or medical device in the ŠÚKL database.

name: Li/SvDH
definition: A methodology developed by Livsmedelsföretagen (Li) and Svensk Dagligvaruhandel (SvDH), based on a report and established standards from RISE (Research Institutes of Sweden AB). The approach employs a screening Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) from cradle to gate, encompassing transport, packaging, and processing stages.

name: Integrated Production of Wine (IPW)
definition:
The Integrated Production of Wine (IPW) is the environmental sustainability scheme established by the South African wine industry. IPW complies with international wine industry environmental sustainability criteria.
This seal is used when the wine is bottled abroad, i.e., not in South Africa.

name: Made for recycling Interzero
definition: Seal from Interzero for environmentally friendly packaging that has been analysed and proven to meet the company’s criteria of recyclability. This includes: recyclable materials, ease of sorting, disposal, etc.

name: Vegan VEG Argentina
definition: VEG Argentina is a third-party certification seal for vegan products, verifying that no ingredients, additives, or processing aids are of animal origin, in accordance with ISO 17030.

name: Fish and seafood traceability
definition: Regulation ensuring full traceability of fish and seafood products throughout the entire value chain — from fisherman or farmer to retail — thereby supporting regulatory compliance, food safety, and sustainable fisheries management. E.g., EU Regulations 1224/2009 and 2023/2842.

name: Public procurement requirements
definition: Requirements established by public procurement agencies, such as the Swedish National Agency for Public Procurement (NAPP), that incorporate environmental and social considerations.

name: Durability index
definition: The durability index indicates the level of repairability and reliability of the product. The criteria taken into account are defined by local regulations. For example, the availability of technical documents, the ease with which the product can be dismantled, the availability of spare parts, the resistance to stress and wear, the ease of maintenance and servicing, the existence of a commercial guarantee, etc.

name: Repairability index
definition: The repairability index indicates the level of repairability of the product. The criteria taken into account are defined by local regulations. For example, the availability of technical documents, the ease with which the product can be dismantled, the availability of spare parts, etc.

name: Beta Pinene
definition: Beta Pinene is a bicyclic monoterpene found in plants like pine needles, rosemary and basil. It has a woody, green, pine like scent. Example: a common terpene in Cannabis. Also known as β-Pinene. CAS number: 127-91-3

name: Farnesene
definition: Farnesene is a sesquiterpene, a type of organic compound found naturally in plants including apples, ginger, basil, grapefruit and cannabis. It is known for its sweet, woody, or fruity aroma and it is a component of various essential oils and natural coatings on fruits like apples. Example: farnesene occasionally found in small concentrations in strains with greater levels of myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and linalool terpenes. Also known as trans-farnesene. CAS number: 502-61-4

name: Terpineol
definition: Terpineol is a monoterpenoid alcohol and it is characterized by a floral, lilac like scent and can be found naturally in various plants including cardamom, cajuput oil, pine oil, and petitgrain oil. Example: a minor terpene in cannabis compared to others like humulene or caryophyllene. CAS number: 8000-41-7

name: Terpinolene
definition: Terpinolene is a terpene found in many plants, including cannabis, sage, apple, cumin, lilac, tea tree, lemon, pine and fir. It is known for its woody, floral and citrus aroma. Example: Terpinolene is more commonly found in sativa strains of cannabis, especially those with higher THC levels. Also known as alpha-terpinolene. CAS number: 58-62-9

name: Trans Caryophyllene
definition: Trans Caryophyllene is natural bicyclic sesquiterpene found in many essential oils, notably from plants used for medicinal purposes. It has a spicy, peppery and woody aroma. Example: a common terpene in cannabis and it is one of the chemical compounds that contributes to the aroma of black pepper. Also known as β-caryophyllene (BCP). CAS number: 87-44-5

name: Do-it-yourself (DIY), garden & pets
definition: A retail channel comprising stores that specialize in home improvement, gardening, and pet-related products. This includes tools, materials, and supplies for repair, maintenance, and crafting; products for gardening, landscaping, and outdoor living; as well as food, accessories, and supplies for pets. Typical examples include hardware stores, garden centers, and pet supply retailers.

name: Fast moving consumer goods (FMCG)
definition: A retail channel focused on fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), also known as consumer packaged goods (CPG) or convenience goods. These are high-turnover products sold quickly and at relatively low cost, such as packaged foods, beverages, toiletries, and household consumables. Examples include supermarkets, hypermarkets, discount retailers, and convenience stores.

name: Tarte
definition: The product has ingredient(s) that causes the flavour/scent of tarte pastry style.

name: Berry
definition: Identifies the berries contained in the product.

name: Phosphorus

name: Sugar, added
definition: Identifies the added sugar contained in the product.
